Active VE52~$200–2501,8002.038 lbsBest value for home detailing
Greenworks 2000 PSI~$150–1802,0001.237 lbsBudget entry point
RYOBI 2300 PSI~$250–300600–2,3001.242 lbsVersatile car + home use
MJJC Foam Cannon Pro V2~$35–45N/A (add-on)N/A2 lbsFoam cannon upgrade

Electric vs. Gas: Why Electric Wins for Car Detailing

Gas pressure washers deliver more PSI (3,000+), but for car detailing they're actually worse:

  • Too much pressure: 3,000+ PSI can strip paint, damage trim, and push water past seals. You'd need to stand much farther back, reducing cleaning effectiveness and foam cannon performance.
  • No auto-stop: Gas units run continuously. Electric units with auto-stop (like the Kranzle TS) shut off when you release the trigger — saving wear, reducing noise, and preventing overheating.
  • Noise: Gas pressure washers are loud enough to anger every neighbor in your building. Electric models are quiet enough to use at dawn in a Miami condo complex without complaints.
  • Exhaust: Can't run a gas pressure washer inside a garage. Electric runs anywhere you have an outlet.

For home car detailing in Miami, electric is the clear choice. Save gas pressure washers for driveway and construction work.

Essential Pressure Washer Accessories for Car Detailing

A pressure washer alone isn't a complete detailing setup. Here's what to add:

Foam Cannon

If your pressure washer didn't come with one, the MJJC Foam Cannon Pro V2.0 (~$35) is the upgrade to make. Thick foam = safer washing.

Microfiber Wash Mitt

After the foam cannon pre-wash, use a plush microfiber wash mitt (not a sponge) for contact washing. The Rag Company Cyclone Wash Mitt (~$15) is the detailing community's favorite.

Filtered Water System

Miami's tap water is hard — loaded with minerals that leave water spots on dark paint. A deionized water filter like the CR Spotless Water De-Ionizing System (~$300–400) attaches to your water line and produces spot-free rinse water. On a dark-colored exotic, this is transformative — you can let the car air dry without a single water spot.

Undercarriage Cleaner Attachment

For flushing salt air deposits from your underbody, an undercarriage cleaner attachment (~$20–30) rolls under the car and sprays upward. In Miami's coastal environment, this should be part of your monthly wash routine.

How to Safely Pressure Wash an Exotic Car

The Two-Bucket + Foam Cannon Method

  1. Pre-rinse: Use the pressure washer with a 40-degree (white) nozzle from 3+ feet away to rinse loose dirt, sand, and debris. Never use the 0-degree (red) nozzle on paint.
  2. Foam: Switch to the foam cannon with a quality pH-neutral car shampoo. Coat the entire car in thick foam and let it dwell for 3–5 minutes.
  3. Rinse foam: Rinse the foam off with the pressure washer. This step alone removes the majority of contaminants without touching the paint.
  4. Contact wash: Using the two-bucket method (one wash, one rinse), gently wash panels from top to bottom with a microfiber mitt.
  5. Final rinse: Rinse with filtered/DI water if available. Otherwise, rinse quickly and dry immediately with a quality drying towel to prevent water spots.
  6. Dry: Use a plush drying towel or a filtered air blower. In Miami's heat, you need to move fast — water evaporates quickly and leaves mineral deposits.

Miami-Specific Tips

  • Wash in shade: Never pressure wash in direct Miami sunlight. The water and soap will dry on the paint faster than you can rinse, leaving spots and streaks. Early morning (before 9 AM) or under a covered parking structure is ideal.
  • Bug removal: South Florida's love bugs (especially April–May and August–September) are acidic enough to etch paint if left for more than 48 hours. A dedicated bug remover spray before the foam cannon step makes quick work of them.
  • Weekly washes: In Miami's environment, washing every 7–10 days prevents salt and contaminant buildup from damaging paint and coatings. A pressure washer makes this a 30-minute task instead of a 90-minute ordeal.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Active VE52 offers the best combination of performance, price, and quiet operation for home detailing. If you want the professional-grade tool that Miami's top detailers trust, the Kranzle K 1622 TS is the buy-it-once-cry-once option that will outlast your car collection. And if you're just getting started, the Greenworks 2000 PSI proves you don't need to spend $500 to properly wash an exotic.

Pair any of these with a quality foam cannon, filtered water, and a good microfiber mitt, and you've got a detailing setup that would make most professional shops jealous. Your Miami exotic's paint will thank you. 💦

title: Best GPS Trackers for Exotic Cars: Protect Your Miami Investment
excerpt: Miami ranks among the top US cities for exotic car theft and insurance fraud. A hidden GPS tracker is the best way to recover your investment if the worst happens. Here are the top GPS trackers for exotic car owners in 2026.
content:
Here's a number that should concern every exotic car owner in Miami: Florida ranks #1 in the US for vehicle theft, and Miami-Dade County is consistently among the state's worst counties. When your car is worth $200K to $2M+, it's not just a vehicle — it's a target. And while alarm systems and steering wheel locks deter opportunists, a GPS tracker is what actually gets your car back when a professional takes it.

We've evaluated the best GPS trackers for exotic cars based on what matters most: real-time accuracy, battery life, tamper resistance, covert installation, geofencing, and the kind of instant alerts that give law enforcement — and you — the edge in recovery situations.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need GPS Tracking

Miami's exotic car theft landscape is uniquely dangerous:

  • Port proximity: The Port of Miami and Port Everglades are two of the busiest shipping ports in the US. Stolen exotics can be loaded into a container and on a ship to South America, the Caribbean, or West Africa within hours of being taken. Once it's on a boat, it's gone. A GPS tracker is the only way to intercept before that happens.
  • Relay theft: Modern keyless-entry exotics (virtually all of them in 2026) are vulnerable to relay attacks, where thieves use signal amplifiers to trick the car into thinking the key fob is nearby. The car unlocks and starts without breaking a single thing. This has been documented on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, Porsches, and Range Rovers in Miami.
  • Valet risk: Miami's valet culture means your keys are regularly in someone else's hands. A GPS tracker with geofence alerts tells you immediately if your car leaves an authorized area — like the restaurant parking lot you're currently sitting in.
  • Insurance requirements: Some high-value vehicle insurers (Chubb, AIG, Hagerty) offer premium discounts for vehicles with active GPS tracking systems. On a $10,000+/year exotic car policy, that discount can effectively pay for the tracker.

Best GPS Trackers for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. LandAirSea Overdrive — Best Overall for Exotic Cars

Price: ~$30 device + $20–25/month service | Battery: Up to 1 year (magnet mount) | Update Rate: Real-time (3-second intervals)

The LandAirSea Overdrive is the tracker that private investigators, fleet managers, and car enthusiasts trust most. It's remarkably small (about the size of a deck of cards), waterproof, and has a built-in magnet mount strong enough to hold onto any metal surface under your car at highway speeds.

What makes it ideal for exotic cars:

  • Real-time tracking: 3-second location updates mean law enforcement can track your car block by block. No 30-second or 1-minute delays that let thieves disappear.
  • Geofencing: Set virtual boundaries around your home, office, or favorite restaurants. Get an instant push notification if your car crosses the boundary — invaluable for valet monitoring.
  • Speed alerts: Set speed thresholds and get alerts if someone is driving your car faster than allowed. Useful for valet monitoring and if a family member borrows the car.
  • 1-year battery: In the extended-life magnetic mount, the Overdrive runs for up to a year on a single charge. No hardwiring required, meaning zero risk of electrical issues in your exotic's sensitive systems.

Best for: Most exotic owners. The combination of price, battery life, and real-time accuracy is unmatched.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Bouncie Smart Driving Companion — Best OBD-II Plug-In Tracker

Price: ~$80 device + $8/month service | Battery: Vehicle-powered (OBD-II) | Update Rate: Real-time (15-second intervals)

The Bouncie plugs directly into your car's OBD-II port (the diagnostic port under the dashboard) and draws power from the vehicle — meaning no batteries to charge, ever. It provides real-time GPS tracking plus vehicle diagnostics: engine codes, battery voltage, coolant temperature, and driving behavior analysis.

For exotic car owners, the diagnostic features add a layer of value beyond tracking. You can monitor your car's health remotely — useful if it's in storage, at a service center, or being driven by someone else. The $8/month service fee is the lowest of any real-time tracker on the market.

The caveat: OBD-II trackers are visible and can be unplugged by a knowledgeable thief. For maximum security, pair a Bouncie with a hidden magnetic tracker like the LandAirSea Overdrive — belt and suspenders.

Best for: Daily-driven exotics where vehicle diagnostics and affordable monitoring are priorities.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Spytec GL300 GPS Tracker — Best Covert Option

Price: ~$30 device + $17–25/month service | Battery: Up to 2.5 weeks (rechargeable) | Update Rate: Real-time (5-second intervals)

The Spytec GL300 is one of the smallest GPS trackers available — about the size of your thumb. It can be hidden virtually anywhere: inside a door panel, under a seat, in the trunk lining, or tucked into the engine bay. Its diminutive size makes it nearly impossible for a thief to find and disable, even if they're looking.

The trade-off is battery life — about 2.5 weeks on a single charge with frequent updates. You can extend this to several weeks by reducing update frequency to every 60 seconds, but for real-time theft recovery, you want the faster intervals.

Spytec's app is excellent, with geofencing, speed alerts, trip history, and SOS notification features. The monthly service is competitive at $17–25 depending on the plan.

Best for: Owners who want a truly hidden tracker that's nearly impossible to detect and disable.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Apple AirTag (with Holder) — Best Supplemental Tracker

Price: ~$29 device + $0/month | Battery: ~1 year (CR2032) | Network: Apple Find My (crowd-sourced)

Let's be clear: an Apple AirTag is not a GPS tracker. It doesn't have GPS. It uses Apple's Find My network — the billion+ Apple devices in the world — to crowd-source its location. In a city like Miami, where iPhones are everywhere, this actually works remarkably well. Location updates come every few minutes as nearby Apple devices anonymously relay the AirTag's position.

The AirTag's strengths are its tiny size, zero monthly cost, and 1-year battery life. Hide one (or several) in your exotic's door panels, trunk, and interior, and you have a backup tracking layer that works independently of cellular-based trackers. If a thief finds and disables your primary tracker, the AirTags continue reporting.

The limitations: Location accuracy is lower (within a block vs. within a few feet for GPS). Updates are not real-time. And Apple's anti-stalking features will alert the thief's iPhone that an "unknown AirTag is traveling with you" after a period of time — though by then, law enforcement should already be notified.

Best for: A supplemental backup layer alongside a primary GPS tracker. At $29 with no monthly fee, there's no reason not to add a few to your exotic.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. CARLOCK Anti-Theft System — Best for Real-Time Driver Alerts

Price: ~$60 device + $10/month service | Battery: Vehicle-powered (OBD-II) | Update Rate: Real-time

CARLOCK is specifically designed as an anti-theft and driver monitoring system rather than a simple tracker. It plugs into your OBD-II port and provides real-time alerts for:

  • Engine start: Get a push notification the instant your car's engine starts — even if it's 3 AM.
  • Unusual vibration: Detects if your car is being towed or loaded onto a flatbed.
  • Device disconnection: Alerts you immediately if someone unplugs the tracker from the OBD-II port.
  • Unusual driving: Flags aggressive acceleration, hard braking, and driving patterns that don't match your profile — useful for valet monitoring.

The vibration detection is particularly valuable for Miami exotic owners. Flatbed theft — where a tow truck simply loads your car — is a growing method for stealing high-end vehicles because it bypasses steering locks and wheel boots entirely. CARLOCK detects the movement and alerts you before the truck pulls away.

Best for: Owners who want proactive theft prevention alerts, not just post-theft tracking.

→ Check price on Amazon

GPS Tracker Comparison Table

TrackerDevice CostMonthly FeeBattery LifeBest Feature
LandAirSea Overdrive~$30$20–25Up to 1 yearReal-time + long battery life
Bouncie~$80$8Vehicle-poweredOBD diagnostics + cheapest service
Spytec GL300~$30$17–25~2.5 weeksUltra-compact, truly covert
Apple AirTag (4-pack)~$29/each$0~1 yearNo monthly fee, backup layer
CARLOCK~$60$10Vehicle-poweredVibration/tow detection

Our Recommended Setup for Miami Exotic Owners

For maximum protection, we recommend a layered approach:

  1. Primary tracker: LandAirSea Overdrive hidden in a covert location (inside a bumper, under the dash, etc.) — real-time GPS with year-long battery life.
  2. Alert system: CARLOCK on the OBD-II port for instant engine start, tow, and disconnect alerts.
  3. Backup layer: 2–3 Apple AirTags hidden throughout the car as a secondary tracking network that works even if cellular trackers are jammed or disabled.

Total cost: roughly $150 in devices + $30/month in service. For a car worth $200K+, that's a rounding error compared to the peace of mind — and the dramatically improved odds of recovery if the worst happens.

Installation Tips for Exotic Cars

Where to Hide a GPS Tracker

The best hiding spots are areas a thief won't check in the critical first 30 minutes:

  • Inside the rear bumper: Most exotics have accessible space inside the rear bumper fascia. The LandAirSea Overdrive's magnetic mount attaches directly to any metal bracket.
  • Behind interior trim panels: Door cards, center console trim, and trunk lining panels can often be removed to tuck a tracker behind them.
  • Inside the spare tire well: If your exotic has one (many don't, but SUVs like the Urus do), it's a classic hiding spot.
  • Engine bay: In a waterproof enclosure, tucked away from heat sources. Less ideal due to extreme temperatures, but very difficult for thieves to access quickly.

Professional Installation

For hardwired trackers or complex installations, consider professional help. Several Miami shops specialize in covert vehicle security:

  • Most authorized exotic dealership service departments will install trackers during routine service
  • Mobile installation services can come to your home or office for discrete setup

Do GPS Trackers Lower Insurance Premiums?

Yes — potentially significantly. High-value vehicle insurers increasingly factor GPS tracking into their risk assessment:

  • Hagerty: May offer premium reductions for vehicles with documented tracking systems
  • Chubb Private Client: Actively considers vehicle security measures including GPS tracking in premium calculations
  • Pure Insurance: Has been known to require GPS tracking on vehicles above certain value thresholds

Ask your insurer specifically. Even a 5% premium reduction on a $12,000/year exotic car policy saves $600 annually — more than covering the cost of a GPS tracker subscription.

Legal Considerations in Florida

In Florida, it is legal to install a GPS tracker on a vehicle you own. If you're tracking a vehicle owned by someone else (even a spouse), the legality becomes murky — consult an attorney. For exotic car owners tracking their own vehicles, there are no legal barriers. Just don't forget to mention the tracker to your insurance company — the disclosure may help your rates.

Bottom Line

In Miami, the question isn't whether you need a GPS tracker on your exotic car — it's which one. The LandAirSea Overdrive is our top pick for most owners, offering the best combination of real-time tracking, battery life, and value. Layer it with Apple AirTags as backup and a CARLOCK for instant alerts, and you have a security system that gives you — and law enforcement — the best possible chance of recovering your investment.

A $30 tracker protecting a $300,000 car. The math speaks for itself. 📍

title: McLaren Senna: The Ultimate Track Hypercar You Can Own
excerpt: With just 500 units built, the McLaren Senna is one of the most extreme road-legal hypercars ever made. Here's everything you need to know about buying, owning, and driving one in Miami.
content:
The McLaren Senna is not a car you buy to cruise down Ocean Drive. Named after the greatest Formula 1 driver who ever lived, the Senna was designed with one singular purpose: to be the fastest McLaren around a racetrack while still wearing a license plate. With only 500 units ever produced and a current market hovering between $1.2 million and $2.5 million depending on spec and mileage, the McLaren Senna has cemented itself as one of the most collectible hypercars of the modern era.

McLaren Senna Specs and Performance

At the heart of the McLaren Senna sits a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 producing 789 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque. That power routes through a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission to the rear wheels, launching the car from 0 to 60 mph in just 2.7 seconds and on to a top speed of 211 mph. But raw speed isn't the Senna's party trick — downforce is. The Senna generates up to 1,764 pounds of downforce at 155 mph, more than any road-legal McLaren before it. The massive rear wing, aggressive front splitter, and sculpted bodywork all serve aerodynamic function over aesthetic form.

SpecificationMcLaren Senna
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 (M840TR)
Horsepower789 hp @ 7,250 rpm
Torque590 lb-ft @ 5,500 rpm
0-60 mph2.7 seconds
Top Speed211 mph
Weight (Dry)2,641 lbs
Downforce1,764 lbs at 155 mph
Transmission7-Speed Dual-Clutch (SSG)
Production500 units
Original MSRP~$958,966
Current Market Value$1.2M – $2.5M+

Why the McLaren Senna Is Special

McLaren has built faster cars (the Speedtail) and more exclusive ones (the Sabre), but the Senna occupies a unique space in the lineup. It's the distillation of McLaren's racing DNA into a street-legal package with zero compromises. The carbon fiber monocoque chassis — called the Monocage III — weighs just 200 pounds and provides the structural foundation for the entire car. The body panels are all carbon fiber too, and McLaren even used carbon fiber for the roof scoop and engine bay cover. The dry weight of 2,641 pounds is absurdly light for a car this powerful.

The suspension is a double-wishbone setup front and rear with adaptive dampers linked to McLaren's RaceActive Chassis Control II system. In Track mode, the car lowers itself and stiffens to a degree that would be punishing on public roads — which is by design. The Senna wants to be on a track. It tolerates the road.

McLaren Senna Driving Experience

Reviews from professional drivers consistently describe the Senna as telepathic. The hydraulic steering provides feedback that most modern cars have engineered out. The brakes — carbon ceramic discs clamped by six-piston calipers up front and four-piston units at the rear — can haul the car from 124 mph to a dead stop in just 100 meters. Visibility is surprisingly good for a hypercar, thanks to the dihedral doors with their glass panels that McLaren calls "teardrop" windows, and the glass panels built into the lower door sections.

The interior strips away everything unnecessary. There's no infotainment touchscreen, no leather-wrapped dashboard, no luxury pretensions. The seats are carbon fiber shells with minimal padding. The door pulls are fabric straps. Climate control exists but is basic. Every gram saved from the interior went toward making the car faster on track. If you want comfort, buy a GT. The Senna is a weapon.

McLaren Senna Variants

Beyond the standard Senna, McLaren produced a few special variants worth knowing about:

  • McLaren Senna GTR: The track-only version. With 814 horsepower, a longer and wider body, and unrestricted aerodynamics, the GTR generates even more downforce and is significantly faster on circuit. Only 75 were made, and prices start around $3.5 million on the secondary market.
  • McLaren Senna LM: Just 20 units produced, created by McLaren Special Operations (MSO) to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the F1 GTR's 1995 Le Mans victory. Each was painted in one of five heritage liveries. These rarely trade hands, but when they do, they command north of $3 million.
  • McLaren Senna Can-Am: Another MSO special, limited to 20 cars, inspired by the legendary Can-Am racing series. Unique liveries and interior touches distinguish these from standard Sennas.

McLaren Senna for Sale: What to Know

If you're shopping for a McLaren Senna in the Miami area, here's the reality. Inventory is thin — at any given time, there might be five to ten available nationwide through dealers and private sellers. Miami-based dealers like The Collection in Coral Gables and Prestige Imports in North Miami Beach occasionally have Sennas in stock. Online platforms like DuPont Registry, Bring a Trailer, and Exotic Car Trader are the best places to monitor availability.

McLaren Senna Price Guide (2026)

Condition / SpecEstimated Price Range
Standard Senna, 1,000+ miles$1.2M – $1.5M
Standard Senna, under 500 miles$1.5M – $1.8M
MSO-spec / unique livery$1.8M – $2.5M
Senna GTR (track-only)$3.5M – $5M+
Senna LM$3M – $4M+ (rarely listed)

Owning a McLaren Senna in Miami

Miami is arguably the best city in America to own a hypercar. No state income tax, year-round driving weather, and a culture that celebrates automotive excess. But a few practical considerations apply to the Senna specifically:

  • Insurance: Expect to pay $15,000 to $30,000 annually for full coverage, depending on your driving record and agreed value.
  • Maintenance: Annual service costs run $3,000 to $5,000 for standard maintenance. Major services (every three years) can exceed $10,000. The carbon ceramic brakes cost over $20,000 to replace — but they last a long time with normal use.
  • Storage: The Senna sits very low (under 4 inches of front ground clearance), so driveways with steep angles are a problem. Many Miami owners keep theirs in climate-controlled garages at facilities like Curated in Wynwood or Gotham Dream Garage in the Design District.
  • Track access: Homestead-Miami Speedway and the soon-to-expand Palm Beach International Raceway give Senna owners nearby circuits to actually use the car as intended. Several track-day organizations run regular events at both venues.

McLaren Senna vs. the Competition

The Senna's direct rivals — the Ferrari FXX-K Evo (track only), Aston Martin Valkyrie, and Mercedes-AMG One — each take a different approach to the ultimate performance car. The Senna's advantage is its relative simplicity. No hybrid system, no electric motors, just a twin-turbo V8, lightweight construction, and insane aerodynamics. That simplicity translates to reliability and lower running costs compared to hybrid hypercars, and it makes the driving experience more visceral and connected.

Is the McLaren Senna a Good Investment?

The Senna has appreciated steadily since its original MSRP of approximately $959,000. Low-production McLarens with motorsport heritage tend to hold value well, and the Senna checks every box: named after a legend, limited to 500 cars, lauded by every journalist who drove it, and never likely to be repeated. Most automotive market analysts consider the Senna one of the safer blue-chip hypercars, though values can fluctuate with the broader collector car market.

For Miami collectors building a portfolio of significant cars, the Senna is a strong anchor alongside models like the Porsche 918 Spyder and Ferrari LaFerrari. It's not just a car — it's a piece of McLaren racing history made street legal.

title: Pininfarina Battista: Miami's Next Electric Hypercar
excerpt: The Pininfarina Battista is a 1,877-horsepower all-electric hypercar that perfectly fits Miami's luxury lifestyle. Here's the full breakdown on specs, pricing, and what it's like to own one in South Florida.
content:
The Pininfarina Battista is what happens when one of the most legendary design houses in automotive history decides to build the most powerful Italian car ever made — and make it fully electric. With 1,877 horsepower, a 0-60 time under two seconds, and a starting price of approximately \.2 million, the Battista is not just an electric hypercar. It's a statement about where the future of extreme performance is heading. And in Miami, where electric vehicle culture is booming alongside the city's love affair with exotic cars, the Battista fits right in.

Pininfarina Battista Performance Specs

The numbers are staggering. Four electric motors — one per wheel — produce a combined 1,877 horsepower and 1,696 lb-ft of torque. That makes the Battista more powerful than a Bugatti Chiron. The sprint from 0 to 60 mph takes less than 1.9 seconds, and the car reaches 186 mph in under 12 seconds. Top speed is electronically limited to 217 mph. The 120-kWh battery pack delivers an estimated range of approximately 300 miles on the WLTP cycle, though aggressive driving will significantly reduce that. DC fast charging capability means the battery can go from 20% to 80% in roughly 25 minutes.

SpecificationPininfarina Battista
PowertrainQuad Electric Motors (AWD)
Total Horsepower1,877 hp
Total Torque1,696 lb-ft
0-60 mphUnder 1.9 seconds
Top Speed217 mph (limited)
Battery Capacity120 kWh
Estimated Range~300 miles (WLTP)
Weight4,681 lbs
Production150 units
Starting Price~\.2 million

Pininfarina Battista Design: Art on Wheels

Pininfarina has been designing cars since 1930 — shaping some of the most beautiful Ferraris, Maseratis, and Alfa Romeos in history. The Battista is their first car as a manufacturer, not just a design consultancy, and they poured nine decades of aesthetic mastery into it. The silhouette is dramatic but cohesive: flowing lines, a low-slung profile, and active aerodynamic elements that deploy based on speed and driving mode. The front features a signature Pininfarina curve that flows from the nose over the front fenders and down the body sides.

Inside, the cabin is handcrafted in Italy with materials that include sustainable leather alternatives, anodized aluminum, and carbon fiber. Every Battista is essentially bespoke — the company offers a personalization program called "Battista Bespoke" with virtually unlimited color and material combinations. The wraparound cockpit features a driver-focused layout with two digital screens — one for the instrument cluster and one for ancillary functions — plus a minimalist center console with rotary drive mode selectors.

Why the Pininfarina Battista Fits Miami

Miami's relationship with electric vehicles is evolving fast. Tesla dominates the roads, Lucid has a studio in Boca Raton, and Rimac — whose technology underpins the Battista — has been gaining recognition through collaborations with Porsche and Bugatti. The Battista slots into Miami's luxury scene as something genuinely different from the Ferraris and Lamborghinis that dominate the usual valet lines on South Beach.

  • Zero emissions, maximum presence: The Battista turns heads without making a sound. In a city that recently cracked down on loud exhaust in South Beach entertainment districts, an electric hypercar that still looks like a spaceship is a compelling proposition.
  • Charging infrastructure: Miami-Dade County has been expanding its EV charging network aggressively. Luxury condos in Brickell and Miami Beach are adding high-speed chargers to parking garages, and Electrify America stations along I-95 and the Turnpike provide DC fast charging for longer drives.
  • Climate advantage: Unlike cold-weather cities where EV range suffers in winter, Miami's warm climate is actually ideal for battery performance and range consistency year-round.
  • Car culture fit: Miami collectors already own cars from rare marques. Adding the first all-electric Italian hypercar to a collection that includes a Ferrari, Lamborghini, and Pagani makes a statement about forward-thinking taste.

Pininfarina Battista Pricing and Availability

Only 150 Battistas will ever be built, making it significantly rarer than the McLaren Senna (500 units) or even the Ferrari LaFerrari (499 units). Pricing starts at approximately \.2 million before personalization, which can add several hundred thousand dollars depending on spec. Deliveries to US customers began in late 2023 and are ongoing, with the production run expected to complete by 2026 or early 2027.

Pininfarina operates a direct sales model — there are no traditional dealerships. The company has brand experience spaces in key markets. In the US, the closest touchpoint for Miami buyers is through Pininfarina's North American operations. Several Miami-based exotic car dealers have listed pre-owned Battistas as well, though secondary market inventory remains extremely thin given the car's newness and limited production.

Pininfarina Battista Cost of Ownership

Expense CategoryEstimated Annual Cost
Insurance (Agreed Value)�,000 – �,000
Charging (10,000 mi/yr)� – \,000
Maintenance\,000 – \,000
Storage (Climate-Controlled)\,000 – \8,000
Registration & Tax,000+ (first year)

Pininfarina Battista vs. Rimac Nevera

The elephant in the room: the Rimac Nevera. Rimac supplies the core electric powertrain technology for the Battista, and the Nevera uses a similar quad-motor setup with 1,914 horsepower. They're related but distinct. The Nevera is a Croatian engineering showcase — raw, tech-forward, and brutally fast. The Battista is an Italian design statement built on that same technological foundation. Think of it this way: if the Nevera is a Formula 1 car, the Battista is the concours d'elegance entrant. Both are extraordinary. The Battista just wraps the performance in more emotional, sculptural bodywork. For Miami, where aesthetics matter as much as specs, that distinction is meaningful.

Pininfarina Battista Driving Modes

The Battista offers five driving modes, each adjusting power delivery, regenerative braking, suspension stiffness, and stability control:

  • Calma: Reduced power output for relaxed cruising. Ideal for Miami Beach traffic.
  • Pura: Balanced performance for everyday driving. Full power available but with softer throttle mapping.
  • Energica: Sharpened responses and firmer suspension. The sweet spot for spirited driving on A1A.
  • Furiosa: Maximum power, minimum intervention. Track mode essentially.
  • Carattere: Fully customizable — choose your own combination of powertrain, chassis, and stability settings.

Is the Pininfarina Battista Worth It?

At \.2 million, the Battista competes with some of the most exclusive hypercars on Earth. What it offers that combustion rivals don't is genuine technological novelty combined with handcrafted Italian artistry. The Battista is the first car to carry the Pininfarina badge as a standalone manufacturer — that alone gives it historical significance. For collectors who already have a garage full of V8s and V12s, adding an electric hypercar with this level of exclusivity (150 units worldwide) represents both diversification and a bet on the direction performance cars are heading.

For Miami owners specifically, the Battista makes even more sense than it does in most markets. The warm climate optimizes battery performance, the charging infrastructure keeps improving, the quiet operation sidesteps noise enforcement, and the sheer visual drama of the car ensures it stands out even in a city drowning in Lamborghinis. If you're in a position to acquire one, the Pininfarina Battista might be the most forward-thinking addition to a Miami exotic car collection in 2026.

title: Fastest 0-60 Cars You Can Buy in Miami Right Now (2026)
excerpt: From under 2 seconds to barely over 3, these are the fastest 0-60 cars available at Miami dealerships in 2026 — with real pricing, specs, and where to find them.
content:
Miami is a city that worships speed. Between the wide-open straightaways of the Dolphin Expressway, the coastal stretches of A1A, and the proximity to Homestead-Miami Speedway, owning a fast car here isn't just a flex — it's practically a civic duty. If you're shopping for the fastest 0-60 car you can actually buy at a Miami dealership in 2026, this is your definitive guide. We've ranked the quickest production cars on sale right now by their 0-60 mph times, with real-world pricing and where to find them in South Florida.

Fastest 0-60 Cars Ranked: The Complete 2026 List

Every car on this list is a production vehicle available for purchase through authorized dealers or direct sales in the Miami area. No one-off concepts, no prototypes, no "manufacturer claims" without independent verification. These are the fastest 0-60 cars money can buy right now.

The Sub-2-Second Club: Fastest 0-60 Cars That Defy Physics

The sub-two-second 0-60 club used to be theoretical. Now four production cars can do it, and all of them are available in Miami. The Rimac Nevera holds the crown at 1.85 seconds — a time so fast that most humans physically cannot process the acceleration before it's already happened. The Pininfarina Battista, built on similar Rimac technology, is a fraction behind at 1.86 seconds but wraps the performance in Italian design that arguably looks better doing it. The Lucid Air Sapphire, a sedan that seats four adults in luxury, hits 60 in 1.89 seconds and might be the most practical car on this entire list. And the Tesla Model S Plaid cracks the barrier at 1.99 seconds for under 0,000, making it the bargain of the century in this company.

What all four share: electric powertrains. The instant torque delivery of electric motors is what makes sub-2-second launches possible without destroying transmissions or melting clutches. For Miami buyers, this also means zero emissions, silent operation (useful with South Beach noise enforcement), and surprisingly low running costs relative to their performance.

Best Value: Fastest 0-60 Car Per Dollar Spent

If you want the fastest 0-60 time for the least money, the Tesla Model S Plaid is untouchable. At 9,990, you get a sub-2-second car that also has Autopilot, a massive touchscreen, and enough cargo space for a Costco run. The Porsche Taycan Turbo GT offers 2.1 seconds for 30,000 — still expensive, but with Porsche build quality and handling that embarrasses cars costing twice as much. The Dodge Charger Daytona EV won't win any 0-60 contests against the top of this list, but 3.3 seconds in a muscle car for under 5K is remarkable.

Where to Buy the Fastest 0-60 Cars in Miami

Miami is one of the best cities in the country for buying extreme performance cars. Here's where to find the cars on this list:

  • The Collection (Coral Gables): Authorized Porsche, McLaren, Ferrari, and Aston Martin dealer. Your one-stop shop for the Taycan Turbo GT, McLaren 750S, and Ferrari SF90 XX.
  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach): The go-to Lamborghini dealer in South Florida. They handle the Revuelto and can source allocation-only models.
  • Braman Motors (Miami): Porsche, BMW, and other premium brands. Strong Taycan inventory.
  • Tesla Miami (Doral & Aventura): Two Tesla locations for the Model S Plaid. Inventory typically available for immediate delivery.
  • Lucid Studio (Boca Raton): The closest Lucid location for Air Sapphire orders. About 45 minutes north of Miami.
  • Curated Miami: Independent exotic dealer that occasionally stocks Rimac, Bugatti, and other hypercars on consignment.

Fastest 0-60 Car for Miami Streets vs. Track Days

There's a difference between the fastest 0-60 car on paper and the one that's actually best to drive in Miami. On public roads, the Tesla Model S Plaid and Lucid Air Sapphire are the most usable — they're comfortable, quiet, have good visibility, and won't get you pulled over for exhaust noise. The Porsche Taycan Turbo GT splits the difference between daily driver and track weapon beautifully.

For track days at Homestead-Miami Speedway or the soon-to-open Miami Autodrome, the McLaren 750S and Ferrari SF90 XX are in a different league. Their mid-engine layouts, advanced aerodynamics, and track-focused suspension tuning make them significantly faster over a full lap than the electric sedans, even if the EVs win the drag race to 60. The Lamborghini Revuelto, with its new V12 hybrid powertrain, offers the best of both worlds — brutal straight-line speed with the visceral engine note that makes track days unforgettable.

Electric vs. Gas: The 0-60 War Is Over

The data is clear: electric cars dominate the 0-60 leaderboard in 2026. Four of the five fastest cars on this list are fully electric, and the fifth (Ferrari SF90 XX) is a plug-in hybrid. Pure combustion engines simply cannot deliver torque as instantaneously as electric motors. That said, 0-60 time is one metric. Top speed, sustained performance over multiple laps, weight management, and driving engagement are areas where combustion and hybrid cars still hold advantages. The Bugatti Chiron Super Sport, for instance, tops out at 273 mph — a figure no electric car has matched.

For Miami buyers, the practical takeaway is this: if you want the fastest car from stoplight to stoplight, buy electric. If you want the most complete high-performance driving experience, the hybrid hypercars from Ferrari and Lamborghini still deliver something that pure EVs don't — a sensory experience that goes beyond raw numbers.

What About the Fastest 0-60 Car Under 00K?

Not everyone has 00K for a Lamborghini. For budget-conscious speed freaks in Miami, these are the fastest 0-60 options under six figures:

  • Tesla Model S Plaid (9,990): 1.99 seconds. Nothing else comes close at this price.
  • Dodge Charger Daytona EV (3,595): 3.3 seconds with American muscle styling.
  • BMW M3 CS (13,000): Slightly over 00K, but 3.2 seconds with a twin-turbo straight-six that sounds incredible.
  • Chevrolet Corvette Z06 (15,000): 2.6 seconds with a flat-plane crank V8 that revs to 8,600 rpm. Just over budget but worth every penny.

The honest answer: the Tesla Model S Plaid has made the under-00K performance segment almost boring. It's so much faster than everything near its price that the only reasons to buy alternatives are sound, driving feel, or brand preference — which are all valid reasons, especially in Miami.

title: Lamborghini for Sale in Miami: The Complete 2026 Buyer's Guide
excerpt: Every Lamborghini model currently for sale in Miami — new and pre-owned — with real pricing, dealer info, and what to watch out for. The only guide you need before buying a Lambo in South Florida.
content:
If you want to buy a Lamborghini for sale in Miami, you're in the right city. South Florida has one of the densest concentrations of Lamborghini inventory in the United States, from brand-new Revueltos at the authorized dealer to pre-owned Huracáns at independent exotic lots across Dade and Broward counties. But buying a Lamborghini is not like buying a Toyota — the pricing is opaque, the markups can be brutal, and the wrong purchase can cost you six figures in depreciation within a year. This guide covers every Lamborghini model available in Miami in 2026, where to buy, what to pay, and how to avoid the most expensive mistakes.

Every Lamborghini for Sale in Miami: 2026 Model Lineup

Lamborghini currently produces three model families, plus limited-edition specials that appear on the secondary market. Here's what you'll find at Miami dealers right now:

Authorized Lamborghini Dealers in Miami

There is one authorized Lamborghini dealer in the Miami metro area, and it controls virtually all new-car allocation for South Florida:

  • Prestige Imports — Lamborghini North Miami Beach: Located at 14800 Biscayne Blvd, this is the sole authorized Lamborghini dealer for Miami-Dade County. They handle new vehicle orders, certified pre-owned inventory, factory warranty service, and Ad Personam (custom configuration) orders. If you want a new Lamborghini for sale in Miami with full factory backing, this is where you go.

Being the only game in town means Prestige Imports can — and does — charge significant dealer markups on high-demand models like the Revuelto. Allocations are typically offered to existing customers first. If you're a first-time buyer, expect to either pay over MSRP or wait 12-18 months for a build slot.

Should You Buy From an Independent Dealer?

Miami has dozens of independent exotic car dealers selling pre-owned Lamborghinis. Some of the most reputable include:

  • Curated Miami (Wynwood): High-end consignment with transparent pricing and detailed vehicle histories.
  • Miami Motorcar Collection (Hialeah): Large inventory of pre-owned exotics including Huracáns and Urus models.
  • Exotic Cars of Houston — Miami Branch: National dealer with Miami presence, competitive pricing on pre-owned inventory.
  • iLusso (Coral Gables): Boutique dealer specializing in late-model luxury and exotic cars.

Buying from an independent can save you 0,000-0,000 compared to certified pre-owned pricing at Prestige Imports. The trade-off: no factory certified warranty (though many cars still carry remaining manufacturer warranty), and you need to be more diligent about inspecting the vehicle's history, service records, and condition.

Lamborghini for Sale in Miami: New vs. Pre-Owned Pricing

The Miami exotic car market has its own pricing dynamics that differ from national averages. Demand is consistently high, inventory moves quickly, and seasonal tourism (November through April) creates price spikes as visiting buyers compete with locals.

Cost of Owning a Lamborghini in Miami

The sticker price is just the beginning. Miami Lamborghini ownership comes with recurring costs that can surprise first-time buyers:

  • Insurance: Expect ,000-0,000 per year depending on the model, your driving record, and coverage level. The Urus tends to be cheaper to insure than the Huracán or Revuelto. Miami's insurance rates are already among the highest in the country due to fraud and weather risk.
  • Annual service: Lamborghini's scheduled maintenance runs ,000-,000 per visit. The V10 Huracán is the least expensive to maintain. The Revuelto's hybrid system adds complexity and cost.
  • Tires: High-performance tires for a Huracán or Revuelto cost ,500-,000 for a full set and may last only 8,000-12,000 miles depending on driving style. Miami's hot asphalt accelerates tire wear.
  • Depreciation: This is the biggest cost. A new Urus depreciates approximately 0,000-0,000 in the first year. Huracáns hold value better, especially limited editions. The Aventador has actually appreciated since discontinuation.
  • Florida sales tax: Miami-Dade County charges 7% sales tax on vehicle purchases. On a 00,000 Huracán, that's 1,000.
  • Storage: If your condo doesn't have covered parking, climate-controlled storage runs 00-,500 per month in the Miami area.

Lamborghini for Sale: What to Inspect Before Buying

Whether buying new or pre-owned, there are Lamborghini-specific issues every Miami buyer should know about:

  • Lift system: Almost every Lamborghini sold in Miami needs the front-axle lift system. Miami's speed bumps and parking garage ramps will destroy a lowered Lambo's front splitter without it. If buying used, confirm the lift system is installed and functioning.
  • Salt and humidity damage: Miami's coastal air is corrosive. Check for early corrosion on brake components, exhaust hardware, and suspension bolts — especially on cars that were parked outdoors or near the beach.
  • Rental car history: Many pre-owned Lamborghinis in Miami were previously rental cars. Exotic rental companies in South Beach cycle through Huracáns and Urus models aggressively. Ask for the complete ownership history and look for signs of hard use: interior wear inconsistent with mileage, scuffed wheels, and repainted bumpers.
  • Flood history: Miami flooding is no joke. Always run a vehicle history report and have a pre-purchase inspection check for water intrusion signs — stained carpets, musty A/C, corroded electrical connectors.
  • Ad Personam specs: Custom-configured Lamborghinis hold value better than standard spec cars. Desirable colors (Verde Mantis, Grigio Titans, Blu Cepheus) and carbon fiber packages command premiums on resale.

Best Time to Buy a Lamborghini in Miami

Timing matters. Miami's exotic car market follows predictable seasonal patterns:

  • Best time to buy (May-September): Snowbirds leave, tourist season ends, and dealers sit on inventory longer. You'll find the best deals on pre-owned Lamborghinis during the summer months.
  • Worst time to buy (November-March): Peak season. Northern buyers fly in, Art Basel drives December demand, and the Miami Grand Prix in May creates a spring surge. Markups are highest during these months.
  • End of quarter: Like any car dealer, Lamborghini dealers have quarterly targets. Late March, June, September, and December can yield better negotiating leverage on in-stock inventory.

Financing a Lamborghini in Miami

Most Lamborghini buyers in Miami finance their purchase, even when they could pay cash. Here's the landscape:

  • Lamborghini Financial Services: Factory financing through Prestige Imports. Rates are competitive for well-qualified buyers, and lease options are available with typical terms of 36-48 months.
  • Woodside Credit: Specialist exotic car lender popular in South Florida. They understand exotic car values and offer flexible terms.
  • PNC / Bank of America: Major banks with exotic car lending programs. Typically require 20-30% down payment.
  • Lease vs. Buy: Leasing is popular for the Urus (limits depreciation exposure) while the Huracán and Revuelto are more commonly purchased outright or financed — especially limited editions expected to hold value.

Should You Buy a Lamborghini for Sale in Miami?

Miami is objectively one of the best places in America to own a Lamborghini. No state income tax means more money for the car. Year-round warm weather means year-round driving. The car culture embraces exotics rather than judging them. And the resale market is liquid — when you're ready to sell, there's always a buyer in South Florida.

The main risks are overpaying (especially during peak season or on markup-heavy new models), buying a former rental without knowing it, and underestimating ownership costs. Do your homework on the specific car, get a pre-purchase inspection from an independent Lamborghini specialist, and time your purchase for maximum leverage. A well-bought Lamborghini in Miami isn't just a car — it's a lifestyle asset that holds value better than most luxury purchases.

title: Best Premium Car Covers for Exotic Cars: Protect Your Miami Investment
excerpt: Miami's brutal sun, salt air, and hurricane season make a premium car cover essential for any garaged or outdoor exotic. Here are the best car covers for Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and more in 2026.
content:
Your exotic car's paint doesn't just face threats on the road — it faces them standing still. In Miami, a parked car battles UV radiation strong enough to fade paint in months, salt-laden coastal air that corrodes trim and brightwork, afternoon thunderstorms that leave mineral-heavy water spots, and the occasional hurricane that turns debris into projectiles. A premium car cover is the simplest, most cost-effective way to protect a six- or seven-figure investment when it's not being driven.

We've evaluated the best car covers for exotic cars based on what matters in South Florida: UV protection, breathability (critical in Miami's humidity), water resistance, soft inner linings that won't scratch delicate paint, and custom-fit options for specific exotic models.

Why Miami Exotic Owners Need a Premium Car Cover

Even if your exotic lives in a garage, a cover is essential in Miami. Here's why:

  • UV damage through windows: Many Miami garages have windows or open sides. UV radiation penetrates and degrades paint, rubber seals, and interior materials even in covered parking. A quality cover blocks 99%+ of UV.
  • Dust and debris: Construction dust, concrete dust from parking structures, and general airborne particulate settle on your paint daily. Each speck is an abrasive waiting to scratch when something brushes against it.
  • Humidity and condensation: Miami's 70-80% average humidity means condensation forms on cool surfaces overnight. A breathable cover prevents moisture from pooling on paint while allowing trapped humidity to escape — preventing mold and mildew.
  • Hurricane prep: During hurricane season (June-November), a heavy-duty outdoor cover provides a last line of defense against wind-blown debris when you can't move the car to a hardened structure.
  • Valet and parking protection: A covered car signals "don't touch" to valets, parking attendants, and curious passersby. It's a psychological deterrent as much as a physical one.

Best Car Covers for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. Covercraft WeatherShield HP Custom Car Cover — Best Overall

Price: ~$350–500 (custom fit) | Use: Indoor/Outdoor | UV Protection: Excellent

Covercraft is the gold standard in custom car covers, and the WeatherShield HP is their premium all-weather option. Each cover is cut to the exact dimensions of your specific vehicle — not a generic "fits most sports cars" shape, but a pattern made for a 2024 Ferrari 296 GTB or a 2025 Lamborghini Revuelto specifically. The fit is snug enough to resist wind but loose enough to avoid contact pressure on spoilers and mirrors.

The WeatherShield HP fabric is a single-layer woven material that's remarkably light yet blocks rain, UV, and dust. It breathes well — critical in Miami's humidity — preventing the trapped moisture that causes mold under cheaper covers. The inner surface is soft enough to lay directly on ceramic-coated or freshly polished paint without marring.

Why it's #1 for Miami: The combination of UV blocking, breathability, and water resistance is perfectly suited to South Florida's weather. Custom fit means it protects every contour of your exotic without bunching or flapping in wind.

Best for: Any exotic car owner who wants the best protection available, indoor or outdoor.

2. Coverking Silverguard Plus Custom Car Cover — Best UV Protection

Price: ~$280–400 (custom fit) | Use: Outdoor | UV Protection: Superior

If your exotic sits outdoors — in a driveway, uncovered parking spot, or open-air garage — the Coverking Silverguard Plus is purpose-built for sun-drenched environments. The reflective silver outer layer bounces UV radiation and reduces under-cover temperatures by up to 30°F compared to dark-colored covers. In Miami, where a black car cover can create an oven effect that damages paint and interior, this temperature reduction is significant.

Like Covercraft, Coverking offers custom patterns for specific vehicles. The inner lining is a soft fleece that protects paint from abrasion. It's water-resistant (not waterproof — important distinction for breathability) and includes reinforced grommets for tie-down straps in windy conditions.

Why it works for Miami: The reflective silver surface is specifically designed for high-UV environments. If your car parks in direct Miami sun, this cover reduces heat damage to paint, interior plastics, and rubber seals.

Best for: Exotics that live outdoors or in uncovered parking structures.

3. Platinum Shield Superior Car Cover — Best Heavy-Duty Outdoor Option

Price: ~$200–350 | Use: Outdoor | UV Protection: Excellent

The Platinum Shield is a five-layer cover built for the worst conditions. Its multi-layer construction includes a waterproof membrane sandwiched between UV-resistant outer fabric and a soft fleece inner lining. This is the cover you want for hurricane season — it handles heavy rain, wind-blown debris, and tree sap better than lighter single-layer options.

Semi-custom sizing means it won't fit as precisely as a full custom Covercraft, but the elastic hem and built-in tie-down straps provide a secure fit on most exotic body shapes. It comes with a storage bag and a manufacturer warranty against defects.

Why it works for Miami: Five-layer construction handles the full range of Miami weather — from summer thunderstorm deluges to hurricane-season debris. The heaviest-duty option on this list.

Best for: Outdoor storage in severe weather conditions, hurricane season prep.

4. California Car Cover Multiweave 2 — Best Indoor Cover

Price: ~$250–400 (custom fit) | Use: Indoor | UV Protection: Moderate

If your exotic lives in a climate-controlled garage — as most high-value Miami exotics should — the California Car Cover Multiweave 2 is the premium indoor choice. It's a two-layer woven fabric that's incredibly soft against paint (softer than most microfiber towels), breathable enough to prevent any moisture trapping, and tailored to your specific vehicle.

The Multiweave 2 won't handle heavy rain (it's not designed to), but it excels at what indoor covers need to do: protect against dust, accidental contact, garage debris, and UV that penetrates through windows. Many Miami collectors drape these over their concours-quality cars between shows.

Why it works for Miami: Maximum breathability prevents mold and mildew in Miami's humid garage environments. The ultra-soft lining is safe for the most delicate paint finishes, including matte and satin wraps.

Best for: Garaged exotics, show cars, and collector vehicles that need the gentlest possible protection.

5. Covercraft Evolution Custom Car Cover — Best All-Around Value

Price: ~$200–300 (custom fit) | Use: Indoor/Outdoor | UV Protection: Good

The Covercraft Evolution is the "Goldilocks" option — not as premium as the WeatherShield HP, but significantly better than generic universal covers, at a price that doesn't sting. The four-layer polypropylene construction handles light rain, UV, and dust while remaining breathable and lightweight. Custom fit ensures proper coverage for your specific exotic.

It's an excellent choice for the owner who parks in a covered garage but occasionally needs to leave the car outdoors — at the airport, at a car show, or during a weekend trip. The included storage bag makes it easy to keep in the trunk.

Why it works for Miami: The best balance of protection and price for Miami's mixed indoor/outdoor storage reality. Lightweight enough to apply and remove quickly in parking garages.

Best for: Owners who split time between garage storage and occasional outdoor exposure.

CA Car Cover Multiweave 2$250–400Indoor2✅ ExactGarage queens & show cars

Car Cover Sizing: Why Custom Fit Matters for Exotics

Generic "one size fits all" car covers are the automotive equivalent of wearing someone else's suit. On an exotic car, they're actively harmful:

  • Flapping in wind: A loose cover acts like sandpaper in a breeze, rubbing back and forth across paint with every gust. Miami's afternoon winds and storm gusts can cause real damage to clear coat under a loose cover.
  • Contact pressure: Covers that bunch up over spoilers, mirrors, or air intakes create pressure points. On a ceramic-coated or PPF-wrapped exotic, those pressure points can leave marks.
  • Water pooling: A poorly fitted cover creates pockets where water collects instead of running off. Pooled water + Florida sun = baked-on water spots under the cover.

Custom-fit covers follow every contour — the Urus's roofline, the Huracán's side scoops, the 911 Turbo's whale tail. The fit prevents all three issues and looks professional in a way that signals care to anyone who sees your car.

How to Use a Car Cover Without Scratching Your Exotic

A dirty cover on clean paint defeats the purpose. Follow these rules:

  1. Always cover a clean car: Any dirt on the paint surface will get ground in under the cover. Quick rinse or detail spray wipe before covering.
  2. Keep the cover clean: Machine wash your cover every 3-4 months (most premium covers are machine washable on gentle cycle). In Miami's dusty, pollen-heavy environment, a dirty cover is worse than no cover.
  3. Fold carefully: When removing, fold the cover soft-side-in to prevent the outer surface from touching paint. Never ball it up and toss it in the trunk.
  4. Dry before storing: If the cover is wet from rain, let it dry completely before storing it in its bag. A damp cover in a sealed bag = mildew, especially in Miami's humidity.

Hurricane Season Cover Strategy

During hurricane season (June through November), Miami exotic car owners need a plan. A car cover is one layer of protection, but it's not a substitute for proper storm preparation:

  • If you can evacuate the car: Drive it to a hardened indoor garage away from flood zones. Many Miami storage facilities offer hurricane-rated units — Gotham Dream Garage and similar facilities are built to withstand Category 3+ winds.
  • If the car stays: Use the heaviest-duty cover available (Platinum Shield or equivalent), secure it with tie-down straps, and park in the most protected area of your garage — away from windows and garage doors. Consider wrapping the car in moving blankets under the cover for added debris protection.
  • Post-storm: Remove the cover carefully after the storm. Debris, leaves, and standing water may be on top. Rinse the car thoroughly before any contact wash to remove abrasive particles.

Should You Use a Cover on a Ceramic-Coated or PPF-Wrapped Car?

Absolutely — but with caveats. Ceramic coatings and paint protection film (PPF) protect against chemical and minor physical damage, but they don't block UV degradation of the coating itself. A car cover extends the life of your ceramic coating by reducing UV exposure when the car is parked. Similarly, PPF can yellow over time with UV exposure; a cover slows that process significantly.

The key: use a cover with a soft inner lining (all five options above qualify). Rough inner surfaces can micro-scratch ceramic coatings, which defeats the purpose. The California Car Cover Multiweave 2 and Covercraft WeatherShield HP are particularly gentle on coated surfaces.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Covercraft WeatherShield HP is the move — it handles everything Miami throws at it while being gentle enough for the most precious paint. If your car lives outdoors, the Coverking Silverguard Plus adds reflective UV protection that's invaluable under the South Florida sun. And for garage queens, the California Car Cover Multiweave 2 provides the softest, most breathable protection available.

A $350 cover protecting a $300,000 paint job. The math is simple. Cover your exotic. 🛡️

title: Best Polishing Machines & Kits for Exotic Cars: A Miami Detailing Guide
excerpt: Miami's sun and salt air punish your exotic's paint. A quality polishing machine is how you fight back — removing swirls, restoring gloss, and prepping for ceramic coating. Here are the best polishers for 2026.
content:
Every exotic car in Miami has a secret: under the showroom shine, the paint is taking a beating. UV radiation oxidizes clear coat. Salt air etches microscopic pits. Automatic car washes (the ones you should never use on an exotic) leave swirl marks. Even hand washing with the wrong technique creates fine scratches visible under direct sunlight. The fix? A polishing machine — the single most transformative tool in any detailer's arsenal.

Machine polishing removes those imperfections by leveling the clear coat surface, restoring depth, gloss, and that "wet look" that makes a Ferrari look like it just rolled off the factory floor. It's also the essential prep step before applying ceramic coating — because coating locks in whatever's underneath, good or bad. We've tested and researched the best polishing machines and kits for exotic cars in 2026, with a focus on what works for Miami's unique conditions.

Why Machine Polishing Matters in Miami

Hand polishing is fine for a quick glaze, but it can't correct paint. Only a machine polisher generates the consistent speed, pressure, and heat needed to actually level clear coat imperfections. Here's why Miami exotic owners specifically need one:

  • UV oxidation: Miami's extreme UV index causes clear coat to oxidize faster than almost anywhere in the US. A polishing machine removes the dull, oxidized layer and reveals the fresh, glossy paint underneath.
  • Swirl mark removal: Even careful hand washing creates micro-swirls over time. On dark-colored exotics (Nero Daytona, Obsidian Black, Dark Blue Metallic), these swirls are painfully visible in Miami's intense sunlight. A DA polisher eliminates them.
  • Water spot etching: Miami's hard water and mineral-rich rain leave spots that can etch into clear coat if left untreated. Light machine polishing removes the etching without damaging the surrounding paint.
  • Ceramic coating prep: If you've read our ceramic coating guide, you know that paint correction before coating is mandatory. A polishing machine is how you do that correction.

Dual Action vs. Rotary: Which Polisher for Exotic Cars?

Before we get to specific products, you need to understand the two types of machine polishers:

Dual Action (DA) Polisher — Recommended for Most Owners

A DA polisher oscillates and rotates simultaneously, creating a random orbital pattern that's virtually impossible to burn through paint with. Even if you hold it in one spot too long, the dual action prevents heat buildup that could damage clear coat. This makes it the safe choice for exotic car owners who aren't professional detailers.

Rotary Polisher — For Experienced Users Only

A rotary spins the pad in a single direction, generating more cutting power and heat. In professional hands, a rotary can remove deep scratches and heavy oxidation faster than a DA. In inexperienced hands, it can burn through clear coat in seconds — a $5,000-$15,000 mistake on an exotic with multi-stage factory paint. Unless you have significant polishing experience, stick with a DA.

Best Polishing Machines for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. Rupes LHR21 Mark III BigFoot — Best Overall for Exotics

Price: ~$350–400 | Type: Dual Action (21mm orbit) | Best For: Full paint correction on large panels

The Rupes BigFoot LHR21 is the polisher that professional detailers reach for when working on Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Rolls-Royces — and there's a reason it's the industry standard. The 21mm orbit throws more correction per pass than smaller-orbit machines, meaning you spend less time polishing and reduce the risk of over-working the paint. The electronic speed control maintains consistent RPM under load, so the polisher doesn't bog down mid-panel.

The ergonomics are outstanding. At approximately 5.5 lbs, it's light enough for extended use without fatigue — important when you're spending 4-6 hours correcting an entire exotic. The backing plate and pad system is Rupes' proprietary design, optimized for their BigFoot pads, which are widely available and come in every cutting grade from heavy correction to ultra-fine finishing.

Why it's #1 for Miami: The 21mm orbit is aggressive enough to remove UV oxidation and water spot etching — the two most common paint issues in South Florida — while being safe enough that you won't burn through on your first attempt. Pro detailers in Miami overwhelmingly recommend this machine.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Griot's Garage G9 Random Orbital Polisher — Best Value

Price: ~$130–160 | Type: Dual Action (random orbital) | Best For: Enthusiasts who want pro results on a budget

The Griot's G9 has a cult following in the detailing community, and for good reason. It delivers 80-90% of the Rupes' correction capability at roughly one-third the price. The 6-inch random orbital motion is safe on all paint types, the variable speed dial (2,000-6,800 OPM) gives you precise control, and the 25-foot power cord means you can work around an entire car without an extension cord.

What sets the G9 apart from similarly priced competitors is build quality. The motor is smooth, the bearings are robust, and the vibration is minimal — your hands won't go numb after an hour of use. Griot's also offers a lifetime warranty, which no other polisher in this price range matches.

Why it works for Miami: At $130, it's accessible enough to justify buying even if you only polish your car twice a year. The long power cord is practical for working in Miami garages and outdoor covered parking areas.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Chemical Guys TORQ 22D Random Orbital Polisher Kit — Best Complete Kit

Price: ~$200–250 (full kit) | Type: Dual Action | Best For: First-time polishers who want everything in one box

If you're new to machine polishing and want to unbox a complete system — polisher, pads, compounds, and instructions — the Chemical Guys TORQ 22D Kit is the way to start. The kit typically includes the TORQ 22D polisher, a set of hex-logic pads in multiple cutting grades (heavy, medium, finishing), V-Line compound and polish, microfiber towels, and a pad conditioner. Everything you need to perform a full paint correction, nothing you don't.

The TORQ 22D itself is a capable 22mm orbit dual action machine with digital speed readout and a smooth motor. It's not as refined as the Rupes in terms of ergonomics and vibration damping, but at nearly half the price with a full pad and compound kit included, the value proposition is hard to beat.

Why it works for Miami: First-time Miami exotic owners who've never polished a car before get a complete education in a box. The included pads and compounds are specifically matched to work together, eliminating the guesswork of building a pad/compound combination from scratch.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Rupes LHR15 Mark III BigFoot — Best for Tight Areas

Price: ~$300–350 | Type: Dual Action (15mm orbit) | Best For: Small panels, pillars, bumpers, and tight contours

The LHR15 is the smaller sibling of the LHR21, using a 15mm orbit and a 5-inch backing plate instead of 6 inches. On exotic cars — which are full of complex curves, sharp body lines, and tight spaces between aero elements — this smaller platform is invaluable. It reaches areas the LHR21 simply can't: around mirror housings, between side scoops, along the edge of a Lamborghini's hexagonal styling cues, and into the scalloped surfaces of a McLaren's bodywork.

Many professional detailers own both the LHR21 and LHR15, using the larger machine for flat panels (hood, roof, doors) and the 15 for detail work. If you can only buy one and you own a car with complex bodywork (most exotics), the LHR15 might actually be the better solo choice.

Why it works for Miami: Exotic car bodywork is rarely flat. The LHR15 handles the compound curves of Italian and British supercars better than any full-size polisher.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. Lake Country HDO Polishing Pad Kit — Best Pad Upgrade

Price: ~$60–80 (set of 6) | Compatibility: Fits all 6-inch backing plate DA polishers

No matter which polisher you buy, pads make or break the result. The Lake Country HDO (Heavy Duty Orbital) pads are the aftermarket upgrade that detailing professionals swear by. Made from high-quality foam with an open-cell structure that runs cooler and distributes compound more evenly, they consistently outperform the pads bundled with most polisher kits.

A typical set includes heavy cutting (orange), medium polishing (white), and fine finishing (black) pads. For Miami's most common paint issues — UV oxidation and swirl marks — start with the medium pad and step up to heavy cutting only for deeper defects. Finish with the black pad for maximum gloss.

Best for: Anyone upgrading from factory-included pads. Compatible with Griot's, Chemical Guys, Rupes (with 6" backing plate), and most other DA polishers.

→ Check price on Amazon

Polishing Machine Comparison Table

ProductPriceTypeOrbitWeightBest For
Rupes LHR21 Mark III$350–400DA21mm5.5 lbsPro-grade full correction
Griot's Garage G9$130–160DA (random orbital)Standard6.1 lbsBest value, lifetime warranty
Chemical Guys TORQ 22D Kit$200–250DA22mm5.8 lbsComplete beginner kit
Rupes LHR15 Mark III$300–350DA15mm4.4 lbsTight areas & complex curves
Lake Country HDO Pad Kit$60–80Pads (add-on)N/AN/APad upgrade for any polisher

Essential Compounds and Polishes for Miami Paint Issues

The polisher is the tool; the compound is what does the actual cutting. Here's what works best for South Florida's typical paint problems:

For UV Oxidation and Heavy Swirls

Meguiar's M110 Ultra Cut Compound (~$25) — The industry-standard heavy cutting compound. Removes oxidation, deep swirls, and water spot etching in one or two passes. Diminishing abrasive technology means it starts aggressive and finishes smooth, reducing the need for a follow-up polish on lighter defects.

For Light Swirls and Finishing

Meguiar's M210 Ultra Finishing Polish (~$25) — The companion to M110. After heavy correction, M210 removes the hazing left by the compound and brings the paint to a mirror-like finish. On light-colored exotics with only minor swirls, you can often skip M110 and go straight to M210.

For One-Step Correction

Sonax Perfect Finish 04-06 (~$30) — The one-step wonder. Sonax Perfect Finish cuts like a medium compound and finishes like a fine polish, making it possible to do a complete paint correction in a single step on all but the most damaged paint. It's the secret weapon of detailers who need efficiency without sacrificing results.

How to Machine Polish an Exotic Car: Step by Step

Before You Start

  1. Wash thoroughly: Use a foam cannon and two-bucket method (see our pressure washer guide). Any dirt left on the surface will cause scratching during polishing.
  2. Clay bar: After washing, use a clay bar or clay mitt to remove embedded contaminants — iron particles, tree sap, overspray. The surface should feel glass-smooth before polishing.
  3. Tape off trim: Use painter's tape to protect rubber seals, plastic trim, and badges. Compound residue is difficult to remove from textured surfaces.

The Polishing Process

  1. Apply compound: 3-4 pea-sized drops on the pad. Spread at low speed (speed 1-2) across a 2ft × 2ft section before increasing speed.
  2. Work the section: Increase to speed 4-5. Use overlapping passes (50% overlap) in a crosshatch pattern — horizontal passes, then vertical. Moderate, consistent pressure. Let the machine do the work.
  3. Work until the compound breaks down: You'll see the compound go from opaque to nearly transparent. That's when the diminishing abrasives have finished their job.
  4. Wipe and inspect: Remove residue with a clean microfiber towel. Inspect under a bright LED light (or direct sunlight) at multiple angles. If swirls remain, repeat with the same pad and compound, or step up to a heavier-cutting pad.
  5. Follow with finishing polish: Switch to a finishing pad and fine polish (M210 or equivalent) for maximum gloss.
  6. Final wipe: Use an IPA (isopropyl alcohol) wipe or panel prep spray to remove all oils. This reveals the true correction results and preps the surface for ceramic coating or sealant.

Miami-Specific Polishing Tips

  • Work in shade or garage: Never polish in direct Miami sunlight. The compound dries too fast, creates a haze that's hard to remove, and the polisher can overheat. A climate-controlled garage between 65-80°F is ideal.
  • Morning sessions: If you're working in a non-air-conditioned garage, start early. By noon in Miami's summer, garage temperatures can exceed 100°F — too hot for comfortable polishing and for the compounds to perform optimally.
  • Stay hydrated: This sounds obvious, but polishing an entire exotic car takes 4-8 hours. In Miami heat, dehydration sneaks up fast. Keep water nearby.
  • Don't skip the clay bar: Miami's environment deposits more contaminants on paint than most places — sea salt, iron particles from construction, industrial fallout from the port. Skipping the clay bar step means polishing those contaminants into the paint, causing more damage than you're fixing.

How Often Should You Polish an Exotic in Miami?

Full paint correction (heavy compound + finishing polish) should be done once or twice a year at most. Each polishing session removes a thin layer of clear coat — necessary to eliminate defects, but you don't want to do it excessively. Most factory exotic clear coats are 2-4 mils thick; each polishing pass removes about 0.1-0.5 mils depending on the compound and pad.

Between full corrections, maintain the finish with:

  • Ceramic coating: Applied after correction, lasts 2-5 years, protects the freshly polished surface
  • Spray sealant: Quick monthly application that adds a protective layer over the coating
  • Proper washing: Foam cannon + two-bucket method to avoid reintroducing swirls

If your exotic is ceramic coated and properly washed, you may only need a full machine polish every 18-24 months — even in Miami's harsh conditions.

Professional Polishing vs. DIY in Miami

Professional paint correction on an exotic car in Miami typically runs $500-$1,500 for a one-step polish, or $800-$2,500 for a full multi-stage correction. That's real money, but you're paying for experience, lighting rigs that reveal defects, and the confidence that comes from having corrected hundreds of six-figure paint jobs.

DIY with a Griot's G9 or Chemical Guys TORQ Kit at $130-$250 gets you started for the cost of one professional session. The learning curve is real — expect your first car to take twice as long as an experienced detailer's — but dual-action polishers are forgiving enough that you won't cause damage while learning.

Our recommendation: If you've never polished a car before, start on a less precious vehicle (your daily driver, a family member's car) before touching your exotic. Once you're comfortable with pad selection, compound amounts, and speed settings, you'll have the confidence to tackle your Ferrari or Lamborghini.

Bottom Line

For most Miami exotic owners, the Griot's Garage G9 delivers outstanding results at an accessible price — pair it with Meguiar's M110 and M210 for a correction system that handles UV oxidation, swirl marks, and water spot etching. If you want the tool that Miami's best professional detailers actually use on million-dollar cars, the Rupes LHR21 Mark III is the investment piece that will serve you for decades. And if you want to start with everything in one box, the Chemical Guys TORQ 22D Kit takes the guesswork out of your first paint correction.

In Miami, polishing isn't cosmetic — it's maintenance. Your exotic's paint is under constant assault from the sun, salt, and elements. A quality polishing machine is how you fight back. ✨

title: Aston Martin for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Dealers & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: Looking for an Aston Martin for sale in Miami? Here's every model, current pricing, and which dealers carry them — from brand-new Vantages to pre-owned DB11s.
content:
If you're searching for an Aston Martin for sale in Miami, you're in one of the best cities in the country to find one. South Florida has one of the highest concentrations of luxury and exotic car dealerships in the United States, and Aston Martin has a strong presence here. Whether you want a brand-new 2026 Vantage, a certified pre-owned DB11, or a collector-grade DBS Superleggera, Miami's market has options that most cities simply don't.

This guide covers current Aston Martin pricing for every model available in 2026, the best dealerships in Miami to buy from, and what you need to know before writing that check.

Aston Martin Models & Pricing in Miami (2026)

Aston Martin's current lineup spans grand tourers, sports cars, SUVs, and limited-production hypercars. Here's what each model costs and what you can expect to find on Miami dealer lots right now.

ModelStarting MSRPMiami Market PriceBody Style
Vantage55,00060,000 – 85,000Coupe / Roadster

DBX70739,00045,000 – 75,000Super SUV
