Valkyrie,000,000+,500,000+ (secondary market)Hypercar

Miami Aston Martin prices typically run 3-8% above MSRP on new models due to South Florida's strong demand and limited allocations. Pre-owned models can actually be better deals here because the supply of trade-ins is higher than in most markets — Miami buyers cycle through cars fast.

Best Aston Martin Dealers in Miami

Aston Martin Miami (The Collection)

The Collection in Coral Gables is the official Aston Martin dealer for the greater Miami area and one of the top-performing Aston Martin dealerships in North America. Located at 200 Bird Road, their showroom typically has 20-30 new Aston Martins in stock at any given time, plus a strong selection of certified pre-owned vehicles. If you're buying new and want allocation priority on limited models like the Valhalla, this is where your relationship needs to be. Their service department is factory-certified, which matters when you're dealing with a car that has a hand-built V12.

Prestige Imports

While primarily a Lamborghini dealer, Prestige Imports on South Dixie Highway frequently has pre-owned Aston Martins in their inventory. They're worth checking for DB11s, Vantages, and the occasional DBS that came in on trade. Their pricing on pre-owned Aston Martins tends to be competitive because they're not an Aston franchise and don't carry the brand premium.

Warren Henry Auto Group

Warren Henry in North Miami handles multiple luxury brands and often stocks pre-owned Aston Martins. They've been in the Miami luxury car business for decades and have a solid reputation for straight dealing. Good option if you want to compare an Aston Martin against a Bentley or Range Rover at the same location.

Private Sellers & Consignment

Curated Miami on NW 2nd Avenue specializes in consignment sales of high-end exotics and frequently lists Aston Martins. Bring a Buyer from DuPont Registry is another avenue — many Miami Aston Martin owners list their cars on DuPont before going to a dealer. For pre-owned purchases, always get a pre-purchase inspection (PPI) from an independent Aston Martin specialist before committing.

New vs. Pre-Owned Aston Martin: What Makes Sense in Miami

Aston Martins depreciate significantly in the first 2-3 years. A DB11 that stickered for 20,000 new can often be found pre-owned with under 15,000 miles for 30,000-50,000. That's a massive savings, and the car is still essentially new. Miami's pre-owned market is particularly strong because owners here tend to keep cars in excellent cosmetic condition — garage-kept, detailed regularly, no salt road damage (Florida doesn't salt roads).

The exception is limited-production models. The Valkyrie, Valhalla, and any special-edition DBS will hold value or appreciate. If you can get an allocation on one of these, take it — they're investments as much as they are cars.

Aston Martin Price Trends to Watch in 2026

Several factors are affecting Aston Martin prices in the Miami market right now:

  • DB12 launch effect: The DB12 replaced the DB11, pushing DB11 pre-owned prices down 10-15%. Great time to buy a used DB11.
  • DBX707 demand: The super-SUV segment is white-hot in Miami. DBX707s are selling at or above MSRP with minimal time on lots.
  • Valhalla hype: With deliveries starting in late 2026, allocation holders are already fielding offers above sticker. If you didn't get on the list early, expect to pay a premium on the secondary market.
  • Classic Aston Martins: Vintage DB5s, DB6s, and V8 Vantages from the 1980s continue to climb. Miami's car show circuit has driven demand for these significantly.

Financing an Aston Martin in Miami

Most Miami Aston Martin buyers finance, even when they don't need to. With rates in the current market, many buyers prefer to keep capital invested rather than tying it up in a depreciating asset. The Collection offers in-house financing through Aston Martin Financial Services, typically at 5.9-7.9% APR depending on credit and term. For better rates, check with:

  • Woodside Credit: Specializes in exotic car loans, often has the best rates for high-value vehicles
  • LightStream: Unsecured personal loans up to 00K with competitive rates for excellent credit
  • PNC Premier Banking: Strong presence in South Florida with dedicated exotic car lending

Leasing is another popular option — see our complete Aston Martin lease guide for Miami for current lease deals and terms.

What to Inspect Before Buying a Pre-Owned Aston Martin

Aston Martins are hand-built and beautifully engineered, but they have maintenance needs that differ from mass-market cars. Before buying pre-owned, make sure you check:

  • Service history: Aston Martin service intervals are strict. Missed services can void remaining warranty and signal neglect.
  • Transmission: The automated manual (Sportshift) in older models is a known weak point. Test for smooth shifting and listen for grinding or hesitation.
  • Cooling system: In Miami's heat, cooling system components work overtime. Check for leaks, coolant condition, and fan operation.
  • Paint and clear coat: Florida sun damages clear coat. Inspect for fading, orange peel, and whether the car has been ceramic coated (a good sign).
  • Interior leather: Heat and UV destroy leather. Check for cracking on the dash, door cards, and seats.

Aston Martin Ownership Costs in Miami

Owning an Aston Martin in Miami goes beyond the purchase price. Here's a realistic breakdown of annual ownership costs:

ExpenseAnnual Cost (Estimate)

Tires,500 – ,000

Detailing & Paint Protection,000 – ,500
Parking (if Brickell/Downtown),000 – ,000

Total annual cost of ownership ranges from roughly 2,000 to 5,000 depending on the model and how you use it. Factor this in when budgeting — the purchase price is just the beginning.

Where to Find the Best Aston Martin Deals in Miami

The best time to buy an Aston Martin in Miami is typically late summer through early fall. Dealers are clearing inventory before new model year allocations arrive, and you'll find the most aggressive pricing on outgoing models. End-of-quarter (March, June, September, December) also produces deals as dealerships push to hit volume targets. For pre-owned, keep an eye on Curated Miami, DuPont Registry, and Bring a Trailer — some of the best deals on pre-owned Aston Martins come through consignment and auction rather than traditional dealerships.

title: Aston Martin Valhalla: Specs, Price & What Miami Buyers Need to Know
excerpt: The Aston Martin Valhalla is the brand's first hybrid supercar — a 998-hp mid-engine monster arriving in late 2026. Here's everything about specs, pricing, and getting one in Miami.
content:
The Aston Martin Valhalla is the most important car Aston Martin has built in decades. It's the brand's first mid-engine production car, its first plug-in hybrid, and the bridge between Aston Martin's grand touring heritage and a future defined by electrification and extreme performance. With a combined output of 998 horsepower from a twin-turbo V8 and three electric motors, the Valhalla isn't just an evolution — it's a statement that Aston Martin can compete with Ferrari, McLaren, and Porsche at the absolute top of the supercar pyramid.

For Miami buyers who've been following the Valhalla's development since its debut as the AM-RB 003 concept, the wait is almost over. Production is ramping up at Aston Martin's Gaydon facility with deliveries expected to begin in late 2026. Here's everything you need to know.

Aston Martin Valhalla Specifications

SpecificationDetail
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 (Mercedes-AMG derived)
Hybrid SystemThree electric motors (2 front, 1 rear)
Combined Power998 hp (745 hp V8 + 253 hp electric)
Combined Torque740 lb-ft
Transmission8-speed dual-clutch (DCT)
DrivetrainRear-mid engine, AWD via electric front axle
0-60 mph2.5 seconds
Top Speed217 mph
EV-Only Range~9 miles
BatteryLithium-ion (details TBC)
Curb Weight~3,417 lbs (1,550 kg)
ConstructionFull carbon fiber monocoque
DoorsDihedral (butterfly-style)
Production Run999 units worldwide

Aston Martin Valhalla Price

The Aston Martin Valhalla has a base price of approximately 00,000. However, "base price" is a loose term for a car like this — virtually every Valhalla will be optioned significantly. Aston Martin's Q by Aston Martin personalization program allows buyers to specify bespoke paint colors, interior materials, carbon fiber finishes, and unique design touches that can push the final price well above 00,000.

On the secondary market, expect premiums. With only 999 units being produced and allocations already spoken for at most dealerships worldwide, any Valhalla that hits the resale market before 2028 will likely trade above million. This is following the same pattern we saw with the Ferrari SF90 Stradale, McLaren Speedtail, and Porsche 918 Spyder — limited-run hybrid supercars appreciate immediately when demand exceeds production.

How the Valhalla Compares to Its Rivals

The Valhalla enters a rarefied segment of hybrid supercars. Here's how it stacks up against the competition you'll see parked on Ocean Drive:

CarPower0-60PriceProduction
Aston Martin Valhalla998 hp2.5s00,000+999 units
Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale1,016 hp2.3s50,000+Limited
McLaren W11,258 hp2.7s,100,000+399 units
Porsche 918 Spyder (used)887 hp2.5s,800,000+918 units
Mercedes-AMG ONE1,049 hp2.9s,700,000+275 units

The Valhalla occupies a compelling position: more affordable than the McLaren W1 and AMG ONE, similar power to the Ferrari SF90 XX, and dramatically more exclusive than anything at this price point. For Miami collectors who want a hybrid hypercar without committing million or more, the Valhalla is arguably the smartest play.

Design & Aerodynamics

The Valhalla's design is defined by its aerodynamic function. Every surface, vent, and curve serves a purpose — Aston Martin claims 600 kg of downforce at 150 mph, which puts it in genuine race-car territory. Key design elements include:

  • Active aerodynamics: A rear wing that adjusts angle and height based on speed and driving mode, plus underbody venturi tunnels for ground effect downforce
  • Top-exit exhaust: The exhaust exits through the rear bodywork above the diffuser, keeping underbody airflow clean — a solution borrowed from F1 engineering
  • Dihedral doors: The signature butterfly-style doors hinge forward and upward, making the Valhalla unmistakable in Miami traffic or at a valet stand
  • Carbon fiber monocoque: The entire tub is carbon fiber, keeping weight down despite the hybrid system's battery pack

In terms of visual presence, the Valhalla is lower, wider, and more aggressive than any road-going Aston Martin before it. It looks like nothing else in the lineup — this isn't a GT with hybrid power bolted on. It's a purpose-built supercar that happens to wear an Aston Martin badge.

The Hybrid System Explained

The Valhalla's powertrain is genuinely innovative. The 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 sits behind the cockpit and drives the rear wheels through an 8-speed DCT. Two electric motors on the front axle provide instant torque and all-wheel-drive capability, while a third motor integrated into the transmission fills in torque gaps during gear changes — eliminating the momentary power dip you feel in conventional dual-clutch gearboxes.

The electric-only range of approximately 9 miles might seem modest, but it's enough for short city hops — like driving from your Brickell condo to Komodo without firing up the V8. When you want full performance, all three motors and the V8 work together to deliver that 998 horsepower figure. The system also enables torque vectoring on the front axle, which makes the Valhalla remarkably agile for a car with this much power.

Getting a Valhalla in Miami

If you want an Aston Martin Valhalla in Miami, your primary path is through The Collection (Aston Martin Miami) in Coral Gables. As the authorized Aston Martin dealer for the greater Miami area, they handle all new-car allocations. However, with only 999 units being built globally, securing an allocation is highly competitive.

Here's the reality of getting one:

  • Existing clients first: Aston Martin prioritizes buyers with a purchase history. If you've previously bought an Aston Martin through The Collection, you're in a stronger position.
  • Deposit required: Expect a substantial deposit (typically 0,000-00,000) to hold a production slot, refundable if you back out before spec lock.
  • Spec your car early: Q by Aston Martin personalization takes time. Early allocation holders can spend months choosing colors, materials, and options.
  • Secondary market: If allocations are sold out, your other option is buying a delivery slot from another buyer or purchasing a completed car on the secondary market. Expect a significant premium — potentially 00,000 or more above sticker.

Why the Valhalla Matters for Miami Car Culture

Miami's exotic car scene has historically been dominated by Italian and German brands — Lamborghini, Ferrari, Porsche, and McLaren own the streets. Aston Martin has always had a presence, but more in the grand touring space than the hardcore supercar segment. The Valhalla changes that equation entirely.

A 998-hp hybrid supercar with butterfly doors and a sub-3-second 0-60 time competes head-to-head with anything parked on Ocean Drive. And frankly, it'll stand out more than another Huracán or 911 Turbo S — Miami has thousands of those. A Valhalla? There might be a handful in all of South Florida.

For collectors and enthusiasts, the Valhalla also represents a smart investment. Limited-production hybrid hypercars from this era — the transitional period between pure ICE and full electric — are likely to be highly collectible. The Porsche 918 Spyder, which launched at 45,000, now trades for nearly double that. The Valhalla could follow a similar trajectory.

Aston Martin Valhalla: The Bottom Line

The Aston Martin Valhalla delivers 998 horsepower, a carbon fiber monocoque, hybrid AWD, dihedral doors, and genuine supercar performance for 00,000 — making it one of the most compelling limited-production hypercars on the market. For Miami buyers with the means and the foresight to secure an allocation, it's a car that will define the next chapter of Aston Martin's story and hold serious value for years to come.

If you're serious about getting one, start the conversation with your dealer now. With 999 units worldwide, hesitation is the only thing that guarantees you miss out.

title: McLaren Senna GTR: Specs, Price & Where to Find One in Miami
excerpt: The McLaren Senna GTR takes the already extreme Senna and removes every last road-legal compromise. With only 75 built, it's one of the rarest hypercars in the world — and Miami has a few.
content:
If the McLaren Senna is a track weapon disguised as a road car, the McLaren Senna GTR is what happens when you stop pretending. Built exclusively for the track with zero road-legal requirements, the Senna GTR is McLaren's most extreme production vehicle ever — and one of the most exclusive hypercars on the planet.

McLaren Senna GTR: Key Specifications

SpecificationMcLaren Senna GTRMcLaren Senna (Road)
Engine4.0L Twin-Turbo V84.0L Twin-Turbo V8
Horsepower825 hp789 hp
Torque590 lb-ft590 lb-ft
Weight2,619 lbs (dry)2,641 lbs (dry)
Downforce2,205 lbs at 155 mph1,764 lbs at 155 mph
Transmission7-speed SSG7-speed SSG
Units Built75500
Price (New)$1.4 million$958,966
Current Market Value$1.8–2.5 million$1.2–1.6 million

What Makes the McLaren Senna GTR Different

The Senna GTR isn't just a road Senna with a roll cage bolted in. McLaren's engineering team started from the Senna's carbon fiber monocoque and rebuilt nearly everything around it for pure track performance.

The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 — codenamed M840TR — gets a power bump to 825 horsepower, making it the most powerful McLaren engine at launch. But the real story is aerodynamics. Without road-legal constraints on ride height, wing size, or diffuser depth, McLaren's aero team unlocked 25% more downforce than the road car. At 155 mph, the Senna GTR generates over 2,200 pounds of downforce — enough to theoretically drive upside down on a ceiling.

The suspension is purpose-built for circuit use with race-spec dampers, stiffer springs, and a wider track. The brakes are carbon-ceramic units with race-compound pads. Slick tires come standard. Everything about this car says "I never need to see a speed bump."

McLaren Senna GTR Price and Market Value in 2026

When the McLaren Senna GTR launched in 2019 at $1.4 million, all 75 units sold out immediately. Most went to existing McLaren Ultimate Series collectors — the same clientele who owned P1s, Speedtails, and Elva roadsters.

In 2026, the secondary market tells the story of extreme scarcity. Clean examples trade between $1.8 million and $2.5 million, depending on spec, mileage (or rather, track hours), and provenance. A handful of "delivery-mile" examples with under 100 miles have traded privately above $2.5 million.

For context, the road-legal Senna (500 built) currently trades around $1.2–1.6 million — making the GTR roughly a 50-70% premium over its street sibling.

McLaren Senna GTR in Miami: Where to Find One

Miami's hypercar ecosystem is one of the few places you'll actually encounter a Senna GTR in the wild. Several are known to reside in South Florida collections, and they occasionally appear at private track events at Homestead-Miami Speedway and The Concours Club.

Dealers to watch:

  • Curated Miami — Occasionally sources Ultimate Series McLarens for their private clients
  • McLaren Miami (The Collection) — The authorized dealer; best access to allocation and pre-owned Ultimate Series
  • RMC Miami — Has handled McLaren P1s and Sennas in the past
  • Bring a Trailer / RM Sotheby's — Auction houses where GTRs occasionally surface publicly

If you're serious about acquiring a McLaren Senna GTR, the most reliable path is through McLaren Special Operations (MSO) or by building relationships with authorized McLaren dealers. Most GTR transactions happen privately, well before cars ever appear on public marketplaces.

McLaren Senna GTR vs. the Competition

HypercarPowerWeightUnitsMarket Price
McLaren Senna GTR825 hp2,619 lbs75$1.8–2.5M
Ferrari FXX-K Evo1,036 hp2,535 lbs40$4–6M
Aston Martin Vulcan820 hp2,976 lbs24$3–4M
Lamborghini Essenza SCV12830 hp2,866 lbs40$3.5–5M
Porsche 911 GT1 Evo600 hp2,337 lbs1Priceless

The Senna GTR occupies a unique niche: more extreme than any road car, but more accessible (relatively speaking) than the ultra-limited Ferrari and Lamborghini track programs. It's arguably the best power-to-weight ratio in its class and the most "usable" track-only hypercar — McLaren offers full trackside support and maintenance programs.

Should You Buy a McLaren Senna GTR?

If you have access to a private track (or membership at The Concours Club near Miami), and you want the most visceral driving experience McLaren has ever built, the Senna GTR is in a league of its own. It's lighter, faster, and more aerodynamically extreme than the road Senna, with the kind of mechanical grip that makes professional drivers rethink what they thought was possible.

As an investment, the trajectory is clear. Only 75 exist. McLaren has moved on to the successor generation. The Senna GTR will only become rarer and more collectible over time.

For Miami collectors, it's also a statement piece — the kind of car that anchors a collection and earns respect at any gathering, from Amelia Island to Supercar Saturdays.

title: Lamborghini Sián: Specs, Price & Miami's Rarest Bull
excerpt: The Lamborghini Sián is the brand's first hybrid — a 819 hp V12 supercapacitor hypercar limited to just 63 units. Here's everything Miami buyers need to know about this groundbreaking Lambo.
content:
The Lamborghini Sián isn't just another limited-edition Lambo. It's the car that changed everything for Sant'Agata — the first Lamborghini with hybrid power, the first to use supercapacitor technology instead of conventional batteries, and one of the most visually striking cars the brand has ever produced. With only 63 coupés and 19 roadsters built, the Lamborghini Sián is one of Miami's ultimate unicorn cars.

Lamborghini Sián: Complete Specifications

SpecificationLamborghini Sián FKP 37
Engine6.5L Naturally Aspirated V12 + Electric Motor
Combined Power819 hp (602 kW)
V12 Output774 hp at 8,500 rpm
Electric Motor34 hp (48V supercapacitor)
Torque531 lb-ft
0-60 mph2.8 seconds
Top Speed217+ mph
Weight3,472 lbs (dry)
Transmission7-speed ISR automated manual
DrivetrainAll-wheel drive
Units Built (Coupé)63
Units Built (Roadster)19
Original MSRP$3.6 million

Why the Lamborghini Sián Matters

The "Sián" name means "flash of lightning" in Bolognese dialect — fitting for a car that represents Lamborghini's electrified future. But unlike most hybrids that use heavy lithium-ion battery packs, the Sián uses a supercapacitor integrated directly into the transmission housing.

This supercapacitor technology — developed in partnership with MIT — is three times more powerful and three times lighter than a lithium-ion battery of equivalent output. It charges and discharges instantly, providing instant torque fill during gear changes and a boost off the line. The result: the most powerful Lamborghini ever built at launch, with the naturally aspirated V12 character completely preserved.

For Lamborghini purists who feared electrification would kill the soul of the brand, the Sián was a revelation. The V12 still screams to 8,500 rpm. The electric motor is there to enhance, not replace. It was Lamborghini's proof of concept that hybrid and visceral aren't mutually exclusive.

Lamborghini Sián Price: What It Costs in 2026

Every one of the 63 coupés sold at $3.6 million before options. The 19 Sián Roadsters commanded even more. All were spoken for before the car was publicly unveiled at the 2019 Frankfurt Motor Show — Lamborghini hand-selected buyers from their most loyal collector base.

On the secondary market in 2026, the Lamborghini Sián trades in the $4.5–6 million range for coupés, with roadsters occasionally crossing $7 million in private sales. The combination of extreme rarity (82 total cars worldwide), historical significance, and that glorious V12 hybrid powertrain makes it one of the most collectible modern Lamborghinis.

Lamborghini Sián Design: Inspired by the Countach

The Sián's design draws heavily from the Countach — arguably the most iconic Lamborghini ever made and the car that defined Miami's exotic car culture in the 1980s. The hexagonal taillights, Y-shaped headlights, and aggressive geometric lines are all nods to the Countach DNA, filtered through Lamborghini's modern design language.

Each of the 63 coupés received a unique specification — no two Siáns are identical. Buyers worked directly with Lamborghini's Ad Personam customization team to create one-off color combinations, interior trims, and personalized details. It's the ultimate expression of automotive individuality.

Lamborghini Sián in Miami

Miami and Lamborghini have been inseparable since the Countach era. The Sián continues that legacy as one of the most sought-after cars in South Florida's hypercar ecosystem.

At least two Siáns are known to reside in Miami-area collections, occasionally appearing at exclusive events like The Concours Club's private gatherings and Festivals of Speed. Spotting one on the street is extraordinarily rare — most owners trailer these cars to events.

Where to look if you're buying:

  • Prestige Imports (North Miami Beach) — Lamborghini's authorized Miami dealer with connections to the collector network
  • Curated Miami — Handles ultra-rare hypercar transactions privately
  • RM Sotheby's / Gooding & Company — The major auction houses where Siáns have traded publicly
  • DuPont Registry — Miami's premier luxury marketplace occasionally lists unicorn-level hypercars

Lamborghini Sián vs. Other Hybrid Hypercars

HypercarPowerHybrid TypeUnitsMarket Price
Lamborghini Sián819 hpV12 + Supercapacitor82$4.5–6M
Ferrari SF90 Stradale986 hpV8 + 3 Electric Motors~3,000+$550K–700K
McLaren P1903 hpV8 + Electric Motor375$1.5–2.2M
Porsche 918 Spyder887 hpV8 + 2 Electric Motors918$1.5–2M
Koenigsegg Regera1,500 hpV8 + Electric Motor80$3–4.5M

The Sián occupies a unique position: it's the only V12 hybrid hypercar, the only one using supercapacitor technology, and one of the rarest modern production cars period. While the SF90 offers more raw power and the Koenigsegg Regera pushes higher numbers, nothing else combines Lamborghini's naturally aspirated V12 heritage with hybrid innovation the way the Sián does.

Is the Lamborghini Sián a Good Investment?

With only 82 cars worldwide and values already tracking 30-60% above MSRP, the Sián is one of the safest hypercar investments of the modern era. As Lamborghini transitions fully to hybrid and eventually electric powertrains, the Sián will be remembered as the bridge — the car that proved the brand could evolve without losing its soul.

For Miami collectors, owning a Sián isn't just about the money. It's about having a piece of Lamborghini history that connects the Countach era to whatever comes next. And in a city where Lamborghinis are part of the cultural DNA, that means something.

title: Best Leather Care Kits for Luxury Car Interiors: Miami Owner's Guide
excerpt: Miami's heat and humidity are brutal on leather interiors. Here are the best leather care kits to keep your exotic's cabin looking factory-fresh — from Rolls-Royce Nappa to Lamborghini Alcantara.
content:
Your exotic car's leather interior is quietly suffering in Miami. The combination of 90°F+ heat, relentless humidity, UV exposure through windshields, and the inevitable sunscreen transfer from bare arms is a recipe for cracked, faded, discolored leather. And on a car with a $15,000 interior option package, that's an expensive problem.

We've researched and compared the best leather care kits available in 2026, specifically for the demands of South Florida luxury car ownership. Whether you're maintaining hand-stitched Hermès leather in a Bugatti or keeping a Ferrari's Poltrona Frau hides supple, these kits deliver.

Why Leather Care Is Non-Negotiable in Miami

Leather is skin — and like your own skin, it doesn't love Miami's climate:

  • UV damage: Even with tinted windows, UV rays penetrate and break down leather dyes and finishes. That rich Cuoio tan in your Ferrari will fade to a washed-out beige within 2–3 years without protection.
  • Humidity cycling: Miami's humidity swings from 90%+ outdoors to bone-dry in your air-conditioned garage. This constant expansion and contraction cracks leather over time.
  • Heat absorption: Dark leather in a Miami parking lot can exceed 150°F. That heat accelerates drying, cracking, and dye transfer.
  • Sunscreen and body oils: In Miami, you're getting in and out of your car in shorts and sunscreen year-round. Those chemicals stain and degrade leather faster than almost anything else.

Best Leather Care Kits for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. Leather Honey Complete Leather Care Kit — Best Overall Value

Price: ~$45–55 | Includes: Leather conditioner, cleaner, applicator cloth, microfiber buffing cloth

Leather Honey has been making leather care products since 1968, and their complete kit is the best value proposition in the market. The conditioner is genuinely excellent — it absorbs deeply into leather without leaving a greasy residue, and a single application provides UV protection for up to 6 months.

The cleaner is pH-balanced and safe for all automotive leather types, including the semi-aniline hides found in most modern exotics. It won't strip existing coatings or dyes.

Best for: Most exotic car owners who want reliable protection without overthinking it.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Lexol Leather Cleaner & Conditioner Kit — Best for Routine Maintenance

Price: ~$30–40 | Includes: 16.9oz cleaner, 16.9oz conditioner, applicator sponge

Lexol is the quiet workhorse of leather care. It's what many dealership detail departments actually use (even if they charge you for something fancier). The two-step system — clean first, condition second — is straightforward and nearly foolproof.

The formula is specifically designed for automotive leather and won't interact with the flame-retardant coatings on modern car seats. It's also safe for Alcantara and microsuede when used sparingly with a soft brush.

Best for: Monthly maintenance between deeper treatments. Keep a set in your garage and use it every 3–4 weeks.

→ Check price on Amazon

3. Chemical Guys Leather Complete Care Kit — Best All-In-One System

Price: ~$50–65 | Includes: Leather cleaner, conditioner, leather scented air freshener, applicator pads, brushes

Chemical Guys packages everything you need into one kit — cleaner, conditioner, leather-scented freshener (surprisingly convincing), applicator pads, and a detail brush for stitching and perforations. The cleaner uses a colorless, odorless formula that's safe on all dyed leathers.

What sets this kit apart is the conditioner's vitamin E–enriched formula, which adds UV protection and helps resist the drying effects of Miami's AC-to-heat cycling. It leaves leather feeling natural — not slippery or artificially shiny.

Best for: The person who wants one box that handles everything. Great gift for the car enthusiast in your life.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. Colourlock Leather Repair & Care Kit — Best for Restoration

Price: ~$80–120 | Includes: Mild cleaner, leather shield, filler, color repair, brushes, sponges

If your exotic's leather is already showing damage — scuffs, dye transfer, small tears, or sun fading — Colourlock is the professional-grade solution. This is what high-end restoration shops in Europe use on classic Ferrari and Rolls-Royce interiors.

The kit includes leather filler for small cracks and tears, color-matched repair dye, and their Leather Shield protectant that creates an invisible barrier against UV, dye transfer, and moisture. Application takes more time and skill than basic kits, but the results are transformative.

Best for: Restoring damaged leather on pre-owned exotics, or protecting light-colored interiors (white, cream, tan) that show every mark.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. Furniture Clinic Leather Care Kit — Best Premium Option

Price: ~$90–110 | Includes: Leather cleaner, protection cream, ultra-clean, applicator cloths

Don't let the name fool you — Furniture Clinic's automotive leather products are used by concours-level detailers worldwide. Their Leather Protection Cream is the star: it creates a barrier that repels water, oil, UV rays, and dye transfer while remaining completely invisible and non-tacky.

The Ultra Clean product is particularly useful for Miami owners — it's specifically formulated to remove sunscreen residue, fake tan stains, and ink transfer from denim. If you've ever looked at your Bentley's Magnolia leather and seen blue jean marks, this is the solution.

Best for: Owners of light-colored luxury interiors (Bentley, Rolls-Royce, white Ferrari interiors) who want the highest level of stain prevention.

→ Check price on Amazon

Leather Care Kit Comparison

ProductPriceBest ForUV ProtectionSkill Level
Leather Honey Complete Kit~$50Overall valueYes (6 months)Easy
Lexol Cleaner & Conditioner~$35Routine maintenanceModerateEasy
Chemical Guys Complete Care~$55All-in-one convenienceYes (vitamin E)Easy
Colourlock Repair & Care~$100Damaged leather restorationYes (Leather Shield)Intermediate
Furniture Clinic Premium~$100Light-colored luxury hidesYes (Protection Cream)Intermediate

Leather Types in Exotic Cars: What You're Actually Dealing With

Not all leather is created equal, and knowing what's in your car matters for choosing the right care products:

  • Full-grain / semi-aniline (Ferrari, Lamborghini, Porsche): Premium leather with minimal surface coating. Absorbs products more readily — use conditioner sparingly to avoid darkening.
  • Nappa leather (Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Mercedes-Maybach): Soft, supple, with a light protective coating. Responds beautifully to conditioning. Very susceptible to dye transfer from clothing.
  • Alcantara / microsuede (Lamborghini, McLaren, Porsche GT models): Not actually leather — it's synthetic microfiber. Requires different care: use a dedicated Alcantara cleaner and soft brush. Never use leather conditioner on Alcantara — it'll stain permanently.
  • Poltrona Frau (Ferrari, Maserati): Italian furniture-grade leather sourced from one of the world's finest tanneries. Treat it like the premium material it is — gentle cleaner, quality conditioner, and keep it out of direct sun when possible.

Miami-Specific Leather Care Tips

Window Tint Is Leather Insurance

If you haven't already, get quality ceramic window tint on your exotic. A good ceramic tint (like 3M Ceramic IR or XPEL XR Plus) blocks 95%+ of UV rays and significantly reduces interior temperatures. In Miami, this is the single best thing you can do for your leather after proper care products. Budget $400–800 for a quality tint job on an exotic.

Condition Before Summer, Not After

Most people think about leather care after the damage is done — usually when they notice cracking in October. In Miami, apply a deep conditioning treatment in March/April before the brutal summer UV hits. Think of it like sunscreen: prevention beats treatment every time.

Keep Microfiber Towels in Your Car

Stash a couple of clean microfiber towels in your center console or door pocket. After beach trips, wipe down any exposed leather to remove sunscreen, salt, and moisture before it has time to absorb. This 30-second habit prevents 90% of the staining issues Miami exotic owners deal with.

Garage Humidity Control

If your exotic lives in a garage (even a climate-controlled one in a Brickell high-rise), consider a dehumidifier set to maintain 40–50% relative humidity. This prevents mold growth on leather and eliminates the expansion-contraction cycling that causes cracking. A good 50-pint dehumidifier runs about $200 and pays for itself in preserved interior value.

How Often to Treat Leather in Miami

TaskFrequency (Miami Climate)Time Required
Quick wipe-downWeekly or after each beach trip5 minutes
Full cleaningEvery 2–4 weeks30–45 minutes
Deep conditioningEvery 2–3 months1–2 hours
UV protectant applicationEvery 3–6 months30 minutes
Professional detail (interior)2x per yearDrop-off service

Bottom Line

Your exotic car's leather interior is one of its most expensive and most vulnerable components — especially in Miami. The Leather Honey Complete Care Kit is our top pick for most owners: excellent protection, easy application, and outstanding value. For damaged or neglected leather, Colourlock's repair kit can bring interiors back from the dead. And for Bentley and Rolls-Royce owners with light-colored hides, Furniture Clinic's premium kit offers the best stain prevention money can buy.

Treat your leather like you treat your paint — regularly, proactively, and with the right products. Your resale value (and your back on a hot Miami afternoon) will thank you. 🪑

title: Best Battery Maintainers for Exotic Cars: Keep Your Garaged Miami Supercar Ready to Drive
excerpt: Exotic cars sitting in Miami garages drain batteries fast. Here are the best battery maintainers and tenders to keep your Ferrari, Lamborghini, or Porsche ready to fire up at a moment's notice.
content:
Here's a dirty secret of exotic car ownership in Miami: your car's battery is dying a little every day it sits in the garage. Modern supercars are packed with electronics — alarm systems, ECUs, telemetry modules, keyless entry receivers — that draw power 24/7. Leave a Lamborghini Huracán parked for two weeks without a battery maintainer and you'll be greeted with a dead battery and a $500+ dealer visit to reset the electronics.

A quality battery maintainer (also called a battery tender) costs $50–300 and is the single cheapest insurance policy for your exotic car investment. We've evaluated the best options for the specific demands of high-performance vehicles sitting in South Florida's heat.

Why Exotic Cars Kill Batteries Faster

Your Toyota Camry can sit for a month without issue. Your Ferrari cannot. Here's why:

  • Parasitic draw: Exotic cars have significantly higher parasitic electrical draw than mainstream vehicles. A modern Ferrari draws 30–50 milliamps at rest; a Lamborghini Aventador draws even more. That's enough to drain a battery in 10–14 days.
  • Smaller batteries: To save weight, many exotics use compact lithium-ion or AGM batteries with less reserve capacity than a standard car battery. Less capacity + more draw = faster drain.
  • Heat damage: Miami's garage temperatures (often 85–95°F even with AC) accelerate battery degradation. Heat is the #1 killer of automotive batteries — more than cold — and Miami garages are essentially slow cookers for your battery's chemistry.
  • Infrequent use: Many Miami exotic owners have multiple cars in rotation. A car that sits for 3–4 weeks between drives is a dead battery waiting to happen.

Best Battery Maintainers for Exotic Cars in 2026

1. CTEK MXS 5.0 — Best Overall for Exotics

Price: ~$80–100 | Type: Smart charger/maintainer | Compatibility: 12V lead-acid, AGM, gel, EFB

CTEK is the gold standard in the exotic car world. Ferrari, Porsche, Bentley, and Aston Martin all include CTEK-branded maintainers with their new vehicles — that's not a coincidence. The MXS 5.0 uses an 8-step charging algorithm that analyzes your battery's condition, charges it optimally, and then maintains it indefinitely without overcharging.

The patented desulfation mode is particularly valuable in Miami: heat accelerates sulfation buildup on battery plates, and the MXS 5.0 can reverse early-stage sulfation that would otherwise shorten battery life. It also includes a temperature sensor to adjust charging voltage based on ambient temperature — critical in a hot Miami garage.

Best for: The default recommendation for any exotic car owner. There's a reason the OEMs trust CTEK.

→ Check price on Amazon

2. Battery Tender Plus 1.25A — Best Budget Option

Price: ~$45–55 | Type: Smart charger/maintainer | Compatibility: 12V lead-acid, AGM, gel, lithium

The Battery Tender brand essentially invented the category (it's so ubiquitous that "battery tender" has become a generic term, like "Kleenex"). The Plus model delivers 1.25 amps of charging power — enough to recover a partially discharged exotic battery overnight — and then drops to a float maintenance mode.

It's spark-proof, reverse-polarity protected, and comes with both alligator clips and a permanent ring terminal harness that you can bolt directly to your battery terminals for instant plug-and-play connection. Many exotic owners install the ring terminals once and leave them routed to an accessible point near the front of the car.

Best for: Budget-conscious owners or those maintaining multiple vehicles (buy several and dedicate one to each car).

→ Check price on Amazon

3. NOCO Genius10 — Best for Multi-Vehicle Collections

Price: ~$100–130 | Type: Smart charger/maintainer/repair | Compatibility: 6V and 12V lead-acid, AGM, gel, lithium, deep-cycle

If you've got a multi-car collection — common in Miami — the NOCO Genius10 is the most versatile maintainer on the market. It handles everything from the 6V battery in your vintage Porsche 356 to the lithium-ion unit in your McLaren. The 10-amp output means it can charge faster than most competitors, recovering a dead battery in hours rather than overnight.

The standout feature is NOCO's Force Mode, which can detect and charge batteries down to 1 volt — a lifesaver when a battery has been completely drained by an exotic's parasitic draw. Most smart chargers won't even recognize a battery that dead; the Genius10 will bring it back.

It also includes a built-in battery desulfator and a thermal sensor for automatic temperature compensation — both essential in Miami's heat.

Best for: Collections of 3+ vehicles, mixed vintage and modern, or anyone who wants one charger that does everything.

→ Check price on Amazon

4. CTEK CT5 PowerSport — Best for Lightweight/Lithium Batteries

Price: ~$70–90 | Type: Smart charger/maintainer | Compatibility: 12V lead-acid, AGM, lithium (LiFePO4)

Many modern supercars have moved to lithium-iron-phosphate (LiFePO4) batteries to save weight. The Porsche 911 GT3, McLaren 720S, and Ferrari 296 GTB all offer or include lithium batteries. These require a different charging profile than traditional lead-acid batteries — and using the wrong charger can damage or even destroy them.

The CTEK CT5 PowerSport has a dedicated lithium charging mode that uses the correct voltage curve and cutoff for LiFePO4 chemistry. It's also compact enough to store in a small garage cabinet or even in the car's frunk.

Best for: Any exotic with a factory lithium battery, or owners who've upgraded to aftermarket lithium units like Antigravity or Braille.

→ Check price on Amazon

5. Schumacher SC1281 — Best Heavy-Duty Option

Price: ~$120–150 | Type: Charger/maintainer/engine starter | Compatibility: 6V and 12V, all battery types

The Schumacher SC1281 is overkill for simple maintenance — and that's exactly why some collectors love it. With 100 amps of engine starting power and 30 amps of rapid charging, it can jump-start a dead exotic in an emergency and double as a maintainer for long-term storage.

The built-in microprocessor automatically detects battery type and condition, then selects the optimal charging rate. It includes a large digital display showing real-time voltage, charge percentage, and charging mode — useful data for monitoring battery health over time.

Best for: Garage setups where you want one unit that can maintain batteries AND jump-start a dead car without calling AAA. Also great for owners with larger garaged vehicles like SUVs (Urus, Cullinan) alongside their supercars.

→ Check price on Amazon

Battery Maintainer Comparison

ProductPriceAmpsLithium CompatibleBest For
CTEK MXS 5.0~$905ANo (lead-acid/AGM)Overall best for exotics
Battery Tender Plus~$501.25AYesBudget / multi-car
NOCO Genius10~$11510AYesCollections & versatility
CTEK CT5 PowerSport~$805AYes (dedicated mode)Lithium batteries
Schumacher SC1281~$13530A charge / 100A startYesHeavy-duty / jump start

Installation Tips for Miami Exotic Garages

Permanent Ring Terminal Setup

The best approach for a garaged exotic is a permanent installation:

  1. Attach the ring terminal harness directly to your battery terminals (positive and negative).
  2. Route the connector lead to an accessible point — many owners run it through the front grille or out near a wheel well.
  3. When you park the car, simply plug in the maintainer's quick-connect. No hood opening, no fumbling with clips.

Most battery maintainers include the ring terminal harness. For Ferraris with rear-mounted batteries and front-mounted charge points, the factory charging port works with most maintainers via an adapter.

Power Strip Setup for Collections

For multi-car collections, mount a heavy-duty surge-protected power strip on the garage wall and dedicate one maintainer per vehicle. Label each one. Total cost for maintaining a 4-car collection: about $200–400 in maintainers plus a $30 power strip. Compared to one dealer battery replacement at $500–1,500 per car, it's a no-brainer.

Smart Home Integration

If your Miami home or condo has smart plugs (Kasa, Wemo, or similar), you can plug your maintainer into a smart plug to monitor power draw remotely via your phone. A maintainer drawing steady low wattage means it's in float mode and the battery is healthy. If it's pulling higher wattage constantly, your battery may be failing and needs attention before your next drive.

Miami-Specific Battery Care Tips

AC Your Garage (If Possible)

Battery lifespan roughly halves for every 15°F above 77°F. A non-air-conditioned Miami garage in summer can hit 100°F+, which is actively destroying your battery chemistry. If you're storing a six-figure car, the cost of running garage AC is trivial compared to battery and electronics damage.

Check Battery Health Seasonally

Before Miami's summer heat arrives (April/May), have your battery load-tested at any auto parts store (free) or by your dealer during service. A battery that's marginal in spring will fail in July. Replacement is cheaper and less stressful when you're not stranded at Bal Harbour.

Don't Rely on Short Drives

A 10-minute cruise to South Beach doesn't fully recharge a depleted battery. Modern exotics need 30–45 minutes of continuous driving to bring a battery back to full charge. For weekend warriors, a maintainer is essential — short drives between long rest periods actually accelerate battery wear.

What Happens When an Exotic Battery Dies

On a normal car, a dead battery is a $150 inconvenience. On an exotic, it's a cascade of problems:

  • Ferrari: A fully dead battery can trigger a body computer reset that requires dealer-level diagnostics ($200–500) to clear fault codes.
  • Lamborghini: The Aventador and Huracán use a rear-mounted battery that requires partial disassembly to access. Labor alone for replacement: $300–600.
  • McLaren: McLaren batteries are lithium-ion and replacement units cost $1,200–2,000 from the dealer.
  • Rolls-Royce: Two batteries, complex electrical architecture. A full discharge can corrupt the HVAC and seat memory modules.

A $50–130 maintainer prevents all of this. It's the best ROI in exotic car ownership.

Bottom Line

Every exotic car sitting in a Miami garage needs a battery maintainer. Full stop. The CTEK MXS 5.0 is our top recommendation — it's what the manufacturers themselves trust, and it handles Miami's heat with intelligent temperature compensation. For collections, the NOCO Genius10 offers unmatched versatility. And if budget is the priority, a Battery Tender Plus at $50 is infinitely better than no maintainer at all.

Plug it in. Forget about it. Drive whenever you want. That's the whole point of owning an exotic in Miami. 🔋

title: Lamborghini Huracán STO: Specs, Price & Where to Buy in Miami (2026)
excerpt: The Lamborghini Huracán STO is a road-legal race car with 631 HP and a naturally aspirated V10. Here's everything Miami buyers need to know about specs, pricing, availability, and what it's like to own one in South Florida.
content:
The Lamborghini Huracán STO — Super Trofeo Omologata — is the closest thing to a road-legal race car that Lamborghini has ever built. Born from the Super Trofeo EVO and GT3 racing programs, the Huracán STO strips away luxury pretense and replaces it with carbon fiber, aero wizardry, and a naturally aspirated V10 that screams to 8,500 RPM. For Miami's supercar collectors, it represents the pinnacle of the Huracán lineage — and with production now ended, values are climbing.

Lamborghini Huracán STO Specs & Performance

The Huracán STO uses Lamborghini's legendary 5.2-liter naturally aspirated V10, producing 631 HP and 417 lb-ft of torque. Power routes exclusively to the rear wheels through a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission — making this the most driver-focused, rear-wheel-drive Huracán ever produced.

SpecificationHuracán STO
Engine5.2L naturally aspirated V10
Horsepower631 HP @ 8,000 RPM
Torque417 lb-ft @ 6,500 RPM
DrivetrainRWD (rear-wheel drive only)
Transmission7-speed dual-clutch (LDF)
0-60 MPH3.0 seconds
0-124 MPH9.0 seconds
Top Speed193 MPH
Curb Weight2,952 lbs (1,339 kg)
Weight Savings vs EVO-95 lbs
Downforce Improvement+53% over Huracán Performante

What Makes the Huracán STO Special

Numbers alone don't tell the STO's story. This car was engineered by Lamborghini's Squadra Corse motorsport division — the same team that builds the Super Trofeo race cars and GT3 machines. That DNA shows in every detail:

Aerodynamics Straight from Racing

The STO generates 53% more downforce than the Huracán Performante, thanks to a cofango (combined front fender-hood-bumper unit) inspired by GT3 cars, a massive rear wing with adjustable attack angle, and a fully enclosed underbody. The rear wing alone generates 420 lbs of downforce at 174 MPH. In Miami terms: it's planted through the sweepers at Homestead-Miami Speedway like it's on rails.

Carbon Fiber Everything

Over 75% of the STO's body panels are carbon fiber. The cofango, rear fenders, engine cover, rear bumper, side panels, and even the air intakes are all carbon. Lamborghini uses three different carbon fiber techniques — Sheet Molding Compound (SMC), short-fiber forged composite, and traditional pre-preg — each optimized for the structural and weight demands of each panel.

Three Drive Modes for Street and Track

  • STO (street): Rear-wheel steering active, traction control calibrated for daily driving, MagneRide dampers in comfort. Perfect for cruising Ocean Drive or heading to Supercar Saturdays.
  • Trofeo: Sharpened throttle response, reduced traction intervention, firmer damping. The mode for spirited drives on empty stretches of A1A.
  • Pioggia (rain): Maximum traction and stability control — essential in Miami's sudden summer downpours. The STO's rear-wheel-drive setup demands respect in the wet.

Connected Telemetry System

The STO comes standard with the UNICA telemetry system — essentially the same data logging used in Lamborghini's race cars. It records lap times, g-forces, braking points, throttle application, and driving lines. Data syncs to a dedicated app, so after a track day at Homestead-Miami Speedway or The Concours Club, you can analyze your performance corner by corner.

Lamborghini Huracán STO Price: New vs Used in 2026

The Huracán STO had a base MSRP of approximately $327,838 when new. However, Lamborghini's Ad Personam customization program meant most delivered cars exceeded $380,000–$420,000 with options. With production now ended (the Huracán line was replaced by the Temerario), the STO has entered the collector market.

ConditionPrice Range (2026)Notes
Low-mileage (<1,000 mi)$380,000 – $450,000+Premium for special colors/specs
Under 5,000 miles$330,000 – $400,000Most common on the market
5,000 – 15,000 miles$290,000 – $350,000Best value for drivers
Track-used / higher miles$260,000 – $310,000Inspect carefully; maintenance history critical

Special editions and unique Ad Personam specs command significant premiums. An STO in a one-off color from Lamborghini's custom program can fetch $50,000–$100,000 above comparable standard-color cars.

Where to Buy a Lamborghini Huracán STO in Miami

Miami is one of the strongest markets in the country for the Huracán STO. Here's where to look:

Authorized Lamborghini Dealers

  • Prestige Imports Lamborghini Miami — North Miami Beach. The largest Lamborghini dealer in South Florida and one of the highest-volume in the US. They frequently have pre-owned STOs in inventory and can source specific specs through their network.
  • Lamborghini Broward — Fort Lauderdale. Part of the Warren Henry Auto Group. Another authorized dealer with access to Lamborghini's certified pre-owned program.

Specialty Exotic Dealers

  • Curated Miami — Wynwood. Boutique exotic gallery specializing in investment-grade supercars. They frequently stock low-mileage STOs.
  • RMC Miami — Handles consignment sales for high-end collectors. If you're looking for a specific STO spec, they can often locate it.
  • The Collection — Coral Gables. Multi-brand luxury dealer with an exotic consignment program.

Online Marketplaces

  • DuPont Registry — The classic luxury car marketplace. Always has multiple STOs listed from dealers nationwide.
  • Bring a Trailer — Auction-format sales with full transparency. STO auction results provide the best real-time market data on values.

Owning a Lamborghini Huracán STO in Miami

Insurance Costs

Expect to pay $8,000–$15,000 annually for full coverage on a Huracán STO in Miami, depending on your driving record, garaging situation, and annual mileage. Miami's insurance rates are among the highest in the nation for exotic cars due to theft risk and weather exposure. An agreed-value policy through a specialist like Hagerty or Chubb is strongly recommended over standard carriers.

Maintenance & Running Costs

  • Annual service: $2,000–$4,000 for standard maintenance at an authorized dealer.
  • Tires: The STO runs Bridgestone Potenza Race tires (semi-slick). A full set costs $2,500–$3,500, and they wear quickly if you track the car. Street-focused replacements (Potenza Sport) are $1,800–$2,400 per set.
  • Brakes: Carbon-ceramic brakes are standard. Replacement rotors and pads run $12,000–$18,000 for a full set, but they last 30,000–50,000+ miles with street-only use.
  • Fuel: Expect 13–15 MPG combined. Premium required. Budget $4,000–$6,000 annually depending on mileage.

Miami Climate Considerations

The STO's aggressive aero elements require extra care in Miami's environment. Salt air from ocean proximity accelerates corrosion on exposed carbon fiber edges if not properly sealed. The car's low ride height (even lower than the standard Huracán) means Miami's notoriously bad road surfaces and steep parking garage ramps require constant vigilance. A front-axle lift system is not available on the STO — it was designed for the track, and Lamborghini chose to save weight rather than add convenience.

Huracán STO vs Huracán EVO vs Huracán Tecnica

FeatureHuracán STOHuracán EVOHuracán Tecnica
Horsepower631 HP631 HP (AWD) / 610 HP (RWD)631 HP
DrivetrainRWDAWD or RWDRWD
Weight2,952 lbs3,135 lbs (AWD)3,039 lbs
Aero FocusMaximum downforceBalancedLow drag
Best ForTrack days & collectorsDaily supercarStreet & style
New MSRP (when avail.)~$328K~$262K–$290K~$302K

Is the Lamborghini Huracán STO a Good Investment?

The Huracán STO is widely regarded as one of the best investment-grade Lamborghinis of the modern era, for several reasons:

  • Last naturally aspirated V10: The Temerario replacement uses a twin-turbo V8 with hybrid assist. The STO's screaming NA V10 will never be replicated — making it the end of an era, similar to how the LP 670-4 SV became a blue-chip collectible.
  • Limited production: Lamborghini never disclosed exact STO production numbers, but estimates put it at 1,500–2,500 units globally. Low supply + rising demand from collectors = upward price pressure.
  • Motorsport pedigree: Cars with direct racing lineage historically appreciate better than their road-focused siblings. The STO's Squadra Corse connection is genuine, not marketing.
  • Driving experience: In an era of increasingly heavy, turbo-hybrid supercars, the STO's raw, analog character stands out. Collectors are increasingly valuing "feel" over spec sheets.

For Miami buyers, the STO represents both an extraordinary driving machine and a compelling store of value. If you find one in the right spec at the right price, it's worth serious consideration. 🏁

title: McLaren Price Guide: Every 2026 Model & What Miami Dealers Charge
excerpt: From the entry-level Artura to the million-dollar Senna, here's what every McLaren model costs in 2026 — including real-world Miami dealer pricing, options, and what to expect on the used market.
content:
McLaren has quietly become one of the most popular supercar brands in Miami. Drive through Sunny Isles, Bal Harbour, or Brickell on any given Saturday and you'll spot more McLarens than almost any other exotic marque. There's a reason: McLaren prices offer serious performance-per-dollar value compared to Ferrari and Lamborghini, with a driving experience that many enthusiasts argue is superior to both.

But McLaren's model lineup has evolved significantly, and pricing varies wildly between new, certified pre-owned, and used. Here's the definitive McLaren price guide for Miami buyers in 2026 — covering every current and recent model, real dealer pricing, and where to find the best deals.

McLaren Price List: Every Current Model (2026)

ModelBase MSRPTypical as-Delivered PriceEngineHorsepower
McLaren Artura$237,500$260,000 – $290,0003.0L Twin-Turbo V6 + Electric671 HP (combined)
McLaren Artura Spider$262,500$285,000 – $320,0003.0L Twin-Turbo V6 + Electric671 HP (combined)
McLaren 750S$324,000$360,000 – $420,0004.0L Twin-Turbo V8740 HP
McLaren 750S Spider$349,000$380,000 – $450,0004.0L Twin-Turbo V8740 HP
McLaren W1$2,100,000+$2,500,000+4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 + Electric1,258 HP (combined)

Note: "Typical as-delivered" reflects real-world pricing with common options. McLaren's MSO (McLaren Special Operations) customization can add $30,000–$150,000+ to any model.

McLaren Artura Price & Value in Miami

The McLaren Artura is McLaren's entry-level supercar and represents the brand's most affordable way in. At $237,500 base MSRP, it undercuts the Ferrari 296 GTB ($330,000+) and Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica ($302,000+) by a significant margin — while offering a plug-in hybrid powertrain that delivers 671 combined HP and genuine electric-only driving capability.

For Miami buyers, the Artura makes particular sense:

  • Electric-only mode: 19 miles of EV range means short trips around South Beach or Brickell produce zero emissions and zero engine noise — ideal for early morning departures from residential buildings.
  • Performance: 0-60 in 3.0 seconds, 0-124 MPH in 8.3 seconds. Fast enough to embarrass cars costing twice as much.
  • Fuel economy: The hybrid system delivers 25+ MPG combined — remarkable for a supercar and meaningful when Miami traffic turns your commute into a 45-minute crawl.

Used McLaren Artura Prices (2026)

Early Artura models (2023-2024) are now appearing on the used market at attractive prices as owners trade up to newer specs. Expect to find 2023 Arturas with under 10,000 miles for $185,000–$220,000 — a substantial discount from new and one of the best performance values in the exotic car market.

McLaren 750S Price: The Sweet Spot

The McLaren 750S replaced the 720S and is widely considered the best all-around supercar McLaren has ever built. With 740 HP from the twin-turbo 4.0L V8 (yes, it actually makes 740 HP despite the "750" name referring to PS), the 750S hits 0-60 in 2.7 seconds and tops out at 206 MPH.

The 750S is the volume model you see most often in Miami, and it's the one most buyers cross-shop against the Ferrari F8 / 296 GTB and Lamborghini Huracán.

McLaren 750S Pricing Breakdown

ConfigurationPrice Range

Typical well-equipped Coupe$370,000 – $420,000
Base 750S Spider$349,000
Typical well-equipped Spider$400,000 – $450,000
MSO-loaded / special paint$450,000 – $550,000+

Popular Options That Add Up

  • MSO Defined paint colors: $8,000–$15,000 (MSO Bespoke colors: $25,000–$60,000+)
  • Carbon fiber exterior package: $12,000–$18,000
  • Electrochromic roof (Coupe): $5,500
  • Bowers & Wilkins audio: $5,500
  • MSO carbon fiber interior: $15,000–$30,000
  • Vehicle lift system: $4,200 (essential for Miami's speed bumps and parking garages)

Used McLaren 720S Prices (Predecessor)

The 720S is one of the best used supercar values in Miami right now. With the 750S now established, 720S prices have settled into a sweet spot:

Year / MileagePrice Range

For the money, a used 720S with low miles is arguably the best performance-per-dollar proposition in the entire exotic car market. The 710 HP twin-turbo V8 is the same fundamental engine as the 750S, and the driving dynamics remain world-class.

McLaren W1 Price: The Hypercar Flagship

The McLaren W1 is McLaren's new hypercar flagship — successor to the P1 and Speedtail. With 1,258 combined HP from a twin-turbo V8 and electric motors, it's the most powerful road-legal McLaren ever built. Base pricing starts at approximately $2.1 million, but with MSO options and dealer allocations, expect real-world transaction prices of $2.5 million and up.

The W1 is fully allocated, and secondary market prices are already significantly above MSRP. If you can get an allocation at sticker price, it's an instant six-figure gain. Miami's McLaren dealer — The Collection in Coral Gables — handles allocations based on purchase history and relationship.

McLaren Prices vs Ferrari vs Lamborghini (Miami Market)

SegmentMcLarenFerrariLamborghini
Entry SupercarArtura: $238KRoma: $245KHuracán Tecnica: $302K
Core Supercar750S: $324K296 GTB: $330KHuracán STO: $328K
Flagship HypercarW1: $2.1MSF90 XX: $850K+Revuelto: $608K

McLaren consistently prices at or below its competitors while delivering equal or superior performance. The brand trades on engineering substance over heritage — which appeals to a certain type of Miami buyer who cares more about lap times than badge prestige.

Where to Buy a McLaren in Miami

Authorized Dealer

  • The Collection — McLaren Miami (Coral Gables): The only authorized McLaren dealer in the greater Miami area. They handle new car orders, certified pre-owned, and service. Building a relationship here is essential if you want access to limited-production models like the W1.

Pre-Owned & Specialty Dealers

  • Curated Miami — Wynwood gallery with handpicked McLarens, often in rare specs.
  • RMC Miami — Consignment specialist, frequently lists 720S and 750S models.
  • Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach. While primarily Lamborghini, they often take McLarens on trade.

Online

  • DuPont Registry — Largest selection of McLarens in the Southeast.
  • Bring a Trailer — Auction format provides transparent pricing data. Great for finding specific 720S specs below market.
  • McLaren Certified Pre-Owned — Available through The Collection. McLaren's CPO program includes extended warranty coverage and a multi-point inspection.

McLaren Ownership Costs in Miami

Insurance

McLaren insurance in Miami typically runs:

  • Artura: $5,000–$9,000/year
  • 750S: $7,000–$14,000/year
  • 720S (used): $6,000–$12,000/year

Agreed-value policies through Hagerty or Chubb are recommended. Standard carriers often undervalue McLarens or refuse coverage entirely.

Maintenance

  • Annual service: $1,500–$3,500 depending on service interval.
  • Tires: $2,000–$3,000 per set (Pirelli P Zero or equivalent).
  • Brakes: Carbon-ceramic rotors last 25,000–40,000 miles on the street. Full replacement: $10,000–$16,000.
  • Major service (every 6 years or 36K miles): $5,000–$8,000 including fluid changes and clutch inspection.

Depreciation

McLarens have historically depreciated faster than Ferraris in the first 3 years — roughly 30–40% from MSRP on non-limited models. However, this creates opportunity for used buyers: a 2-year-old McLaren at 60% of its original sticker is an extraordinary performance value. The 720S is currently the poster child for this dynamic, and the Artura is following a similar pattern.

Best McLaren to Buy in Miami Right Now

Our picks for the best McLaren values in the current Miami market:

  • Best overall value: Used 2020-2022 McLaren 720S Coupe ($220K–$260K). Virtually the same performance as the 750S at 35–40% less. The best mid-engine supercar deal in the market.
  • Best new buy: McLaren 750S Spider ($349K base). The Spider adds open-air driving with minimal weight penalty and stronger resale than the Coupe. In Miami's climate, the Spider is the one to have.
  • Best entry point: Used 2023 McLaren Artura ($185K–$210K). Sub-$200K for a McLaren hybrid supercar with the latest tech. Incredible value.
  • Best collector play: McLaren W1 (if you can get one at MSRP). Instant appreciation; the spiritual successor to the legendary P1.

McLaren offers something unique in Miami's supercar landscape: genuine racing technology and engineering excellence at prices that undercut the Italian establishment. Whether you're buying your first exotic or adding to a collection, understanding McLaren pricing in the current market gives you a serious advantage. 🏎️

title: Ferrari Purosangue for Sale in Miami: 2026 Pricing, Dealers & Buyer's Guide
excerpt: The Ferrari Purosangue is Ferrari's first four-door, four-seat GT — and Miami dealers can't keep them in stock. Here's what you'll pay, where to find one, and what every buyer needs to know in 2026.
content:
The Ferrari Purosangue rewrote the rules when it debuted as Ferrari's first-ever four-door vehicle. Now entering its second full model year on the market, the Purosangue has become one of the most sought-after vehicles in South Florida — and finding a Ferrari Purosangue for sale in Miami still requires patience, connections, and a willingness to pay above sticker.

Ferrari Purosangue Price: What Miami Dealers Are Charging in 2026

Ferrari set the Purosangue MSRP at approximately 98,000 before options. But in the real world — especially in Miami — that number is a starting point, not a final price. Here's what the market actually looks like:

If you're seeing a Ferrari Purosangue for sale near MSRP, it's almost certainly an allocated build for an existing client. Walk-in buyers should budget 75K minimum in Miami's current market.

Ferrari Purosangue Specs: What Makes It Special

Under the hood, the Purosangue packs Ferrari's naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 — the same family of engines found in the 812 Superfast. The numbers speak for themselves:

The rear-hinged back doors — often called "suicide doors" — give the Purosangue an unmistakable presence on Collins Avenue or pulling up to Komodo on a Friday night. Despite its GT proportions, it drives like a Ferrari: sharp, engaging, and absurdly fast for a vehicle this size.

Where to Find a Ferrari Purosangue for Sale in Miami

Miami is one of the strongest Ferrari markets in the United States, which is both good and bad news for buyers. Good: there's inventory. Bad: there's competition. Here are your best options:

Authorized Ferrari Dealers

The Collection Ferrari of Coral Gables is Miami's official Ferrari dealer and the primary source for allocated Purosangue builds. If you have an existing relationship and purchase history with Ferrari, this is where your allocation will come from. New clients can join the waitlist, but expect 12-18 months for delivery.

Ferrari of Fort Lauderdale (operated by Holman) is another authorized dealer serving the greater Miami area, roughly 30 minutes north.

Pre-Owned and Independent Dealers

If you don't have a Ferrari allocation and want a Purosangue now, the secondary market is your path. Miami-based dealers frequently listing Purosangue inventory include:

  • Prestige Imports — North Miami Beach, major exotic dealer
  • Curated — Wynwood-adjacent exotic gallery with rotating hypercar inventory
  • DuPont Registry — Online marketplace with dozens of listings, many from Florida sellers
  • iLusso — Costa Mesa-based but ships to Miami regularly

Ferrari Purosangue vs. the Competition in Miami

The Purosangue doesn't exist in a vacuum. Miami's luxury SUV market is crowded, and buyers cross-shop aggressively. Here's how it stacks up:

ModelStarting PriceHP0-60Engine
Ferrari Purosangue98,0007153.3sV12

Bentley Bentayga Speed46,0006263.5sW12
Aston Martin DBX70739,0006973.1sTwin-Turbo V8
Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT94,0006313.1sTwin-Turbo V8

The Purosangue's V12 is its trump card. In a world of turbocharged engines, Ferrari's naturally aspirated twelve-cylinder is an experience no competitor can match. That alone justifies the premium for many Miami buyers.

What to Know Before Buying a Ferrari Purosangue in Miami

Insurance Costs

Expect to pay ,000 – 5,000 annually for comprehensive coverage in Miami-Dade County, depending on your driving record and coverage limits. Florida's no-fault insurance laws and high theft rates push premiums higher than the national average.

Maintenance

Ferrari's 7-year maintenance program covers scheduled service for the first seven years. After that, annual services run ,500 – ,000 depending on the interval. The V12 is reliable but expensive to service — budget accordingly.

Depreciation

Limited production numbers and sustained demand mean the Purosangue is holding value remarkably well. As of early 2026, pre-owned examples are still trading above MSRP. Long-term, expect more modest depreciation than a typical luxury SUV, though the premium over sticker will normalize.

Miami-Specific Considerations

  • Heat: Ceramic coating is essentially mandatory. Miami's sun will destroy unprotected paint.

  • Theft: Miami-Dade has some of the highest vehicle theft rates in the country. A GPS tracker and secured garage are non-negotiable for a 00K+ vehicle.

Is the Ferrari Purosangue Worth It in 2026?

If you want a four-seat Ferrari with genuine supercar performance and the kind of engine that won't exist in five years, the answer is yes. The Purosangue is not an SUV pretending to be a Ferrari — it's a Ferrari that happens to have four doors and enough room for golf bags.

For Miami buyers specifically, it fills a unique niche: fast enough for Saturday morning pulls on I-95, comfortable enough for the drive to Palm Beach, and distinctive enough to stand out even in a city saturated with six-figure SUVs.

The challenge isn't deciding whether to buy one — it's finding one for sale. Start building that dealer relationship now. Your future Purosangue depends on it.
